questions.stem: The researchers found that, despite the initial setbacks, the new drug, when administered in low doses, significantly reduced tumor growth in laboratory mice. The clause "when administered in low doses" is an example of:
opts: A full adverbial clause with its own subject and verb.
A reduced adverbial clause with an implied subject.
A relative clause modifying "the new drug".
A noun clause serving as the object of "found".
questions.explain: 考点：省略结构（状语从句的省略）。"when administered"省略了主语"the new drug"和be动词"it was"，是"when it was administered"的简化形式。

questions.stem: It is the ability to adapt to changing circumstances, rather than raw intelligence, that determines long-term success in most professional fields. Which grammatical structure is used to emphasize "the ability to adapt to changing circumstances"?
opts: Subject-verb inversion
Cleft sentence (It is...that...)
Fronting of the object
Rhetorical question
questions.explain: 考点：强调句型（分裂句）。"It is...that..."是典型的强调结构，用来突出句子的某一成分，这里强调主语"the ability to adapt to changing circumstances"。

questions.stem: The theory, which was first proposed in the 1970s and later refined by subsequent research, continues to influence contemporary thinking in cognitive science. The relative clause "which was first proposed...research" is:
opts: A restrictive clause essential to identifying the theory.
A non-restrictive clause providing extra information.
A clause that functions as the subject complement.
A clause that modifies the verb "continues".
questions.explain: 考点：非限制性定语从句。逗号后的"which"引导非限制性定语从句，对先行词"the theory"进行补充说明，去掉后主句意思仍然完整。

questions.stem: So profound was the impact of the Industrial Revolution that it fundamentally reshaped not only economies but also social structures worldwide. The sentence begins with "So profound" to achieve:
opts: A conditional meaning
A comparative effect
Emphatic effect through inversion
A concessive tone
questions.explain: 考点："so...that..."结构中的倒装。"So + 形容词"置于句首时，主句需要部分倒装（"was the impact"），以强调程度之深。

questions.stem: Having been subjected to rigorous testing over a period of five years, the new vaccine was finally approved for public use by the regulatory authorities. The participial phrase "Having been subjected to rigorous testing over a period of five years" functions as:
opts: A post-modifier of "the new vaccine"
An adverbial of time/reason
A subject complement
An object complement of "approved"
questions.explain: 考点：分词短语作状语。"Having been subjected to..."是现在分词的完成被动式，在句中作时间/原因状语，表示发生在主句动作之前的被动行为。

questions.stem: The phenomenon that the company, which had been struggling for years, finally turned a profit last quarter is a testament to the new CEO's aggressive restructuring strategy. In this sentence, the clause 'that the company...last quarter' functions as a(n) ______.
opts: attributive clause modifying 'phenomenon'
appositive clause explaining 'phenomenon'
subject clause of the main verb 'is'
adverbial clause of result
questions.explain: 考点：同位语从句与定语从句的区分。'that'引导的从句完整陈述了'phenomenon'的具体内容，且'phenomenon'为抽象名词，故为同位语从句；若为定语从句则'that'需在从句中充当成分。

questions.stem: Not until the final report was submitted did the committee realize how deeply the scandal had eroded public trust. Which of the following correctly describes the grammatical structure of this sentence?
opts: It contains a fronted negative adverbial triggering subject-auxiliary inversion in the main clause.
It uses a double negative structure for emphasis.
The main clause is in passive voice with no inversion.
'Not until' introduces a noun clause serving as the subject.
questions.explain: 考点：否定状语前置引起的部分倒装。'Not until...'位于句首时，主句需将助动词'did'提前至主语'the committee'之前，形成部分倒装。

questions.stem: The researchers argue that the data, much of which has been collected over a decade, strongly supports the hypothesis that early intervention can mitigate cognitive decline. How many subordinate clauses are there in this sentence?
opts: Two
Three
Four
Five
questions.explain: 考点：嵌套从句的识别。全句包含：(1)'that the data...decline'为宾语从句；(2)'much of which...decade'为非限制性定语从句；(3)'that early...decline'为同位语从句，共三个从句。

questions.stem: Were it not for the generous scholarship, she would never have been able to attend that prestigious university. The underlined part 'Were it not for' can be best replaced by ______.
opts: If it were not for
If it had not been for
Had it not been for
If it is not for
questions.explain: 考点：虚拟语气的倒装结构。原句为与过去事实相反的虚拟条件句省略'if'后的倒装，'Were it not for'对应'If it were not for'，但题干句意指向过去，'Had it not been for'才是正确时态对应。

questions.stem: What distinguishes this novel from others is not its plot, which is rather conventional, but the way in which the author manipulates language to create a sense of unease. The subject of the main verb 'is' is ______.
opts: 'What distinguishes this novel from others'
'its plot'
'the way'
'the author manipulates language'
questions.explain: 考点：主语从句的识别。'What distinguishes this novel from others'为'what'引导的主语从句，整体作主句的主语，主句谓语为'is'。

questions.stem: The professor insisted that the experiment ______ under strictly controlled conditions, and that all results ______ in detail.
opts: be conducted; be recorded
was conducted; was recorded
conducted; recorded
should conduct; should record
questions.explain: 考点：'insist'后宾语从句的虚拟语气。当'insist'表示'坚持要求'时，宾语从句谓语用'(should+)动词原形'，且主语'experiment'和'results'为动作承受者，故用被动语态'be conducted'和'be recorded'。

questions.stem: So rapidly has technology advanced that what once seemed like science fiction is now an everyday reality. Which of the following is true about the sentence structure?
opts: 'So rapidly' is fronted, causing inversion in the main clause, and 'that' introduces a result clause.
The sentence is a simple sentence with no inversion.
'What once seemed like science fiction' is an adverbial clause.
The main clause is 'technology has advanced', and the rest is a modifier.
questions.explain: 考点：'so...that'结构中'so+adj./adv.'前置引起的倒装。'So rapidly'置于句首，主句主谓部分倒装（has technology advanced），'that'引导结果状语从句。

questions.stem: The CEO, together with his senior advisors, ______ attending the summit, but the flight ______ delayed due to the storm.
opts: is; was
are; was
is; were
are; were
questions.explain: 考点：主谓一致中'就远原则'。主语为'The CEO'（单数），'together with...'为插入修饰语，不影响主语单复数，故第一空用'is'；第二空主语'flight'为单数，用'was'。

questions.stem: It is the ability to adapt to changing circumstances, rather than sheer talent, that determines long-term success in this field. The sentence employs a(n) ______ structure.
opts: emphatic 'it' (cleft sentence)
formal subject 'it'
anticipatory 'it' with a that-clause as subject
dummy 'it' in a passive construction
questions.explain: 考点：强调句（分裂句）的识别。'It is + 被强调部分 + that + 剩余部分'为典型的强调句型，此处强调'the ability to adapt to changing circumstances'，去掉'It is...that'后句子仍完整。

questions.stem: Had the government taken more decisive action earlier, the economic downturn might not have been as severe as it turned out to be. The sentence expresses a ______.
opts: past unreal condition with an implied result in the past
present unreal condition with a future result
mixed condition with a past condition and a present result
future less vivid condition
questions.explain: 考点：虚拟语气中与过去事实相反的假设。'Had + 主语 + 过去分词'为省略'if'的倒装形式，表示与过去事实相反的虚拟条件，主句用'might have been'，为过去虚拟结果。

questions.stem: The phenomenon that the author describes in the passage, which has been widely observed by researchers, ______ a fundamental shift in consumer behavior.
opts: represent
represents
are representing
have represented
questions.explain: 主谓一致：主语中心词是 phenomenon（单数），后接 that 定语从句，谓语动词用单数 represents。

questions.stem: ______ the complexity of the problem, the team decided to adopt a multi-disciplinary approach, drawing on expertise from various fields.
opts: Given
Giving
To give
Having given
questions.explain: Given 为介词，意为'考虑到'，引导原因状语；Giving 为现在分词表主动，不符合逻辑。

questions.stem: The professor, along with his graduate students, ______ conducting a series of experiments designed to test the new hypothesis.
opts: is
are
were
have been
questions.explain: 主谓一致：主语 the professor 为单数，along with... 为插入语，不影响谓语单复数。

questions.stem: Not until the final chapter of the book ______ the author's true intention behind the seemingly random events.
opts: the reader understands
does the reader understand
the reader understood
did the reader understood
questions.explain: Not until 置于句首，主句需部分倒装；且时态为一般现在时，故用 does + 主语 + 动词原形。

questions.stem: The extent to which the new policy will affect small businesses ______ remains to be seen.
opts: it
that
what
questions.explain: 主句主语为 The extent，后接 to which 定语从句，谓语 remains 前无需任何引导词，/ 表示不填。

questions.stem: ______ that the economy would recover so quickly, many investors had sold their stocks prematurely.
opts: Not anticipated
Not anticipating
Not having anticipated
Having not anticipated
questions.explain: 分词短语作原因状语，且动作发生在主句谓语之前，需用完成式；否定词 not 置于 having 之前。

questions.stem: The research, ______ over a decade, finally yielded results that challenged the prevailing theories in the field.
opts: conducting
being conducted
conducted
having conducted
questions.explain: 过去分词 conducted 表被动与完成，相当于 which was conducted，修饰 the research。

questions.stem: So profound ______ that it reshaped the entire discipline's approach to data analysis.
opts: the impact was
was the impact
the impact had
had the impact
questions.explain: So...that 结构将 so + adj 置于句首时，主句需部分倒装：was the impact。

questions.stem: It is the ability to adapt to changing circumstances, rather than raw intelligence, ______ determines long-term success in complex environments.
opts: which
that
what
it
questions.explain: 强调句型 It is...that...，被强调部分为 the ability to adapt to changing circumstances。

questions.stem: The manager insisted that the report ______ before the deadline, despite the team's heavy workload.
opts: be submitted
must be submitted
would be submitted
is submitted
questions.explain: insist 表示'坚持要求'时，宾语从句用虚拟语气 (should) + 动词原形，should 可省略。

questions.stem: The phenomenon that the more we consume, the more we seem to want, which economists call "hedonic adaptation", has been widely observed in modern societies. The underlined clause "that the more we consume, the more we seem to want" functions as a(n) ______ in the sentence.
opts: appositive clause
attributive clause
subject clause
adverbial clause
questions.explain: 该从句位于抽象名词 phenomenon 之后，对 phenomenon 进行内容上的解释说明，是同位语从句，而非定语从句（定语从句需关系词且在从句中充当成分）。

questions.stem: The idea that the government should intervene in the economy, which was once considered radical, has now become mainstream among policymakers. The grammatical function of "that the government should intervene in the economy" is a(n) ______.
opts: attributive clause modifying "idea"
appositive clause explaining "idea"
subject clause of the main sentence
object clause of "considered"
questions.explain: that 从句位于抽象名词 idea 之后，完整说明 idea 的内容，且 that 在从句中不充当成分，因此是同位语从句。

questions.stem: What distinguishes the modern approach from the traditional one is that it emphasizes empirical data rather than theoretical speculation. The subject of the main sentence is ______.
opts: the modern approach
What distinguishes the modern approach from the traditional one
that it emphasizes empirical data
the traditional one
questions.explain: "What distinguishes the modern approach from the traditional one" 是 what 引导的主语从句，在整个句子中充当主语；is 是系动词，后接 that 表语从句。

questions.stem: The researchers found that the subjects who had been exposed to the stimulus for a longer period performed significantly better than those who had not. The clause "who had been exposed to the stimulus for a longer period" is a(n) ______.
opts: restrictive attributive clause modifying "subjects"
non-restrictive attributive clause modifying "subjects"
adverbial clause of time
object clause of "found"
questions.explain: 该从句由关系代词 who 引导，修饰先行词 subjects，且没有逗号隔开，是限制性定语从句，对 subjects 进行限定说明。

questions.stem: The book, which was published in 1998, remains one of the most influential works in the field, although its conclusions have been challenged by recent studies. The clause "which was published in 1998" is a(n) ______.
opts: restrictive attributive clause modifying "book"
non-restrictive attributive clause modifying "book"
adverbial clause of concession
parenthetical clause modifying the whole sentence
questions.explain: which 引导的定语从句前有逗号与主句隔开，对先行词 book 进行补充说明而非限定，是非限制性定语从句。

questions.stem: So pervasive is the influence of social media on young people that many educators have called for stricter regulations. The sentence begins with "So pervasive" to achieve ______.
opts: inversion for emphasis
a question structure
a conditional meaning
a passive voice
questions.explain: "So + 形容词" 置于句首时，主句需部分倒装（系动词 is 提前至主语 the influence 之前），这是为了强调程度之深，属于倒装结构中的强调用法。

questions.stem: Not until the early 20th century did scientists begin to understand the complex mechanisms underlying genetic inheritance. The underlined part "did scientists begin" is an example of ______.
opts: partial inversion caused by negative adverbial at the beginning
complete inversion of subject and verb
emphatic structure "it is...that..."
rhetorical question inversion
questions.explain: "Not until..." 是否定状语置于句首，主句需部分倒装，即助动词 did 提前至主语 scientists 之前，属于部分倒装（主语与助动词倒装，谓语动词仍保留在原位）。

questions.stem: It was the professor's relentless pursuit of truth that inspired generations of students to question established norms. The sentence structure "It was...that..." is used to emphasize ______.
opts: the subject "the professor's relentless pursuit of truth"
the object "generations of students"
the adverbial "to question established norms"
the predicate "inspired"
questions.explain: 该句为强调句型 "It is/was + 被强调部分 + that + 其余部分"，去掉 It was...that 后句子仍完整（The professor's relentless pursuit of truth inspired...），被强调部分是主语 the professor's relentless pursuit of truth。

questions.stem: Had the government taken early preventive measures, the economic crisis would not have escalated to such a devastating level. The underlined part "Had the government taken" is a(n) ______.
opts: inverted conditional clause omitting "if"
past perfect tense in a declarative sentence
subjunctive mood expressing a wish
emphatic structure with "had"
questions.explain: "Had + 主语 + 过去分词" 是 if 条件句的倒装形式，省略 if 并将 had 提前，表示与过去事实相反的虚拟条件（if the government had taken...），属于虚拟语气中的倒装省略结构。

questions.stem: The extent to which the new policy will affect small businesses remains to be seen, but early indicators suggest a mixed impact. The clause "to which the new policy will affect small businesses" is a(n) ______.
opts: attributive clause modifying "extent"
object clause of "remains"
adverbial clause of result
appositive clause explaining "extent"
questions.explain: "to which" 是 "介词 + 关系代词" 结构引导定语从句，修饰先行词 extent，关系代词 which 指代 extent，在从句中作介词 to 的宾语，相当于 "the new policy will affect small businesses to the extent"。

questions.stem: In the sentence "That the brain, once thought to be fixed after childhood, can rewire itself throughout life has been confirmed by a growing body of research.", the subject of the main clause is ______.
opts: the brain
That the brain can rewire itself throughout life
a growing body of research
That the brain, once thought to be fixed after childhood, can rewire itself throughout life
questions.explain: 考点：主语从句作主语。整个"That...life"是主语从句，其中插入"once thought to be fixed after childhood"作定语修饰brain，主句谓语是has been confirmed。

questions.stem: In "The extent to which language shapes thought has long been debated, with some linguists arguing that it determines cognition and others insisting it merely influences it.", the phrase "to which" introduces a(n) ______ clause modifying "extent".
opts: adverbial
relative
noun
elliptical
questions.explain: 考点：定语从句关系词。"to which"引导定语从句修饰先行词extent，相当于"the extent that language shapes thought"。

questions.stem: In "Not until the 20th century did scientists begin to understand the complex mechanisms underlying genetics.", the sentence structure is an example of ______.
opts: partial inversion
full inversion
subject-auxiliary inversion
no inversion
questions.explain: 考点：否定词前置引起的主谓倒装。"Not until..."置于句首，主句需部分倒装（助动词did提前），属于subject-auxiliary inversion。

questions.stem: The sentence "What is now known as the placebo effect was once dismissed as mere imagination, but recent studies have revealed its powerful physiological impact." contains a ______ clause as subject.
opts: relative
adverbial
nominal (noun) clause
comparative
questions.explain: 考点：名词性从句作主语。"What is now known as the placebo effect"是what引导的主语从句（名词性从句），谓语是was dismissed。

questions.stem: In "So profound is the influence of social media on public opinion that traditional news outlets have had to adapt their strategies.", the sentence begins with an inverted structure to emphasize ______.
opts: the subject
the complement
the adverbial
the object
questions.explain: 考点：表语前置引起的倒装。"So profound"是主句表语，前置后主谓倒装（is the influence），目的是强调表语（补足语）。

questions.stem: The sentence "The hypothesis, that early humans migrated across a land bridge, has been challenged by new archaeological findings." contains a(n) ______ clause.
opts: restrictive relative
non-restrictive relative
appositive
adverbial
questions.explain: 考点：同位语从句。"that early humans migrated across a land bridge"是对hypothesis内容的具体说明，且前后有逗号分隔，是同位语从句。

questions.stem: In "Were it not for the discovery of antibiotics, millions more would have died from infections.", the underlined part expresses a ______ condition.
opts: real present
unreal past
unreal present
real future
questions.explain: 考点：虚拟条件句的倒装。"Were it not for..." = "If it were not for..."，表示与现在事实相反的假设（unreal present），主句用would have done表对过去的结果。

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly parses the structure of "The more we learn about the universe, the more we realize how little we know."?
opts: main clause + comparative clause
correlative comparative construction (the...the...)
subordinate clause + main clause with correlative
parallel comparative structure
questions.explain: 考点：the more...the more...比较结构。这是典型的"the + 比较级, the + 比较级"句式，表示"越……越……"，前后两个分句构成平行比较关系。

questions.stem: In "It is not so much that artificial intelligence will replace human workers, but rather that it will transform the nature of work itself.", the phrase "not so much...but rather" functions to ______.
opts: compare two equal ideas
negate the first idea and affirm the second
introduce a cause and effect
express a concession
questions.explain: 考点：固定结构"not so much...but rather"。该结构意为"与其说……不如说……"，否定前半部分（not so much），肯定后半部分（but rather），属于对比强调。

questions.stem: In the sentence "The idea that the function of government is to protect the rights of individuals, which was articulated by Locke, has profoundly shaped modern political thought.", the clause "which was articulated by Locke" is a(n) ______ clause.
opts: restrictive attributive
non-restrictive attributive
adverbial
object
questions.explain: 非限制性定语从句（non-restrictive attributive clause）用逗号与主句隔开，对先行词作补充说明，去掉后不影响句子核心意思。

questions.stem: In "Not until the 19th century did scientists realize that the Earth's magnetic field was not static.", the sentence structure involves ______.
opts: subject-verb inversion after a negative adverbial
a conditional clause
a relative clause with fronted preposition
a passive voice transformation
questions.explain: 否定词（Not until）置于句首时，主句需部分倒装，即助动词did提前，构成"did + 主语 + 动词原形"结构。

questions.stem: In the sentence "What distinguishes humans from other animals is the capacity for abstract reasoning, which enables the development of complex language.", the subject of the main clause is ______.
opts: What distinguishes humans from other animals
the capacity for abstract reasoning
which enables the development of complex language
humans
questions.explain: "What"引导的名词性从句（主语从句）"What distinguishes humans from other animals"充当整个句子的主语。

questions.stem: The sentence "Had it not been for the timely intervention of the central bank, the financial crisis would have spiraled out of control." employs ______.
opts: a mixed conditional
a third conditional with inversion
a first conditional
a second conditional with inversion
questions.explain: 该句为与过去事实相反的虚拟条件句（第三条件句），省略if并将had提前构成倒装，主句用"would have + 过去分词"。

questions.stem: In "The extent to which economic inequality affects social mobility is a question that researchers have long debated.", the phrase "to which" introduces a(n) ______ clause.
opts: attributive
adverbial
object
subject
questions.explain: "to which"引导定语从句修饰先行词"extent"，"to which"在从句中作状语，相当于"the extent that researchers have long debated"的正式表达。

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly identifies the grammatical function of the italicized phrase in "The professor, accompanied by his research team, is expected to deliver a keynote speech."?
opts: a gerund phrase acting as subject
a participial phrase acting as an appositive
a participial phrase acting as a non-restrictive modifier
an infinitive phrase acting as an adverbial
questions.explain: "accompanied by his research team"是过去分词短语，作非限制性定语修饰"The professor"，相当于非限制性定语从句"who is accompanied by his research team"。

questions.stem: In "It is not so much that the data are unreliable as that the methodology is flawed.", the construction "not so much...as..." serves to ______.
opts: compare two equal degrees
emphasize the latter over the former
negate both clauses equally
introduce a concession
questions.explain: "not so much A as B"结构意为"与其说A，不如说B"，强调后者（B）才是更重要的原因或事实。

questions.stem: The sentence "The hypothesis that climate change is primarily driven by human activities, while widely accepted, remains contested by a minority of scientists." contains a(n) ______ clause.
opts: appositive
attributive
adverbial of concession
object
questions.explain: "that climate change is primarily driven by human activities"是同位语从句，对"hypothesis"的内容进行具体说明，而非修饰性定语。

questions.stem: In "Only by integrating diverse perspectives can we hope to address the complex challenges facing modern society.", the inversion occurs because ______.
opts: "Only" + adverbial phrase is placed at the beginning of the sentence
the sentence is a question
the subject is too long
the verb is in passive voice
questions.explain: "Only + 状语/状语短语"置于句首时，主句需部分倒装，即助动词"can"提前至主语"we"之前，形成"can we hope"结构。

questions.stem: The phenomenon that many students, despite having access to vast online resources, still prefer traditional textbooks has puzzled educators for years. 该句中 "that" 引导的从句在句中充当什么成分？
opts: 同位语从句，修饰 phenomenon
定语从句，修饰 phenomenon
主语从句，作整个句子的主语
宾语从句，作 has puzzled 的宾语
questions.explain: that 引导的从句对 phenomenon 进行解释说明，且 that 在从句中不作成分，因此是同位语从句。

questions.stem: Not until the professor had explained the theory three times did the students begin to grasp its complexity. 该句的语法结构特点是什么？
opts: 部分倒装，将助动词 did 提前
完全倒装，将主语 the students 与谓语倒装
强调句型 It is...that... 的省略形式
虚拟语气，表示与过去事实相反
questions.explain: Not until 置于句首时，主句需部分倒装，将助动词 did 提到主语 the students 之前。

questions.stem: The proposal, which the committee had spent months deliberating over, was ultimately rejected by a narrow margin. 句中 "which" 引导的从句是什么类型？
opts: 非限制性定语从句，修饰 The proposal
限制性定语从句，修饰 The proposal
宾语从句，作 had spent 的宾语
状语从句，表伴随状态
questions.explain: which 引导的从句用逗号与主句隔开，对先行词 The proposal 进行补充说明，是非限制性定语从句。

questions.stem: What distinguishes this approach from previous ones is that it integrates both qualitative and quantitative methods seamlessly. 该句的主语是什么？
opts: What distinguishes this approach from previous ones
this approach
that it integrates... seamlessly
both qualitative and quantitative methods
questions.explain: What 引导的主语从句 "What distinguishes this approach from previous ones" 在整个句子中充当主语。

questions.stem: Had it not been for the timely intervention of the mediator, the negotiation would have collapsed entirely. 该句使用了什么语法结构？
opts: 虚拟条件句的省略倒装形式，表示与过去事实相反
过去完成时的正常陈述句式
让步状语从句的倒装形式
强调句型，强调条件状语
questions.explain: Had it not been for... 是 If it had not been for... 的省略倒装形式，表示与过去事实相反的虚拟条件。

questions.stem: The researcher, whose findings were published in a top-tier journal, has been invited to speak at the conference. 句中 "whose" 引导的从句修饰什么？
opts: 修饰 The researcher，表示所属关系
修饰 findings，表示结果
修饰 journal，表示来源
修饰 conference，表示地点
questions.explain: whose 引导定语从句修饰先行词 The researcher，表示 "这位研究人员的" 所属关系。

questions.stem: So profound was the impact of the industrial revolution that it reshaped the entire social structure. 该句的语法结构是？
opts: "so...that..." 结构中的部分倒装，将 so profound 置于句首
完全倒装，主语与系动词完全颠倒
强调句型 It was...that... 的变体
比较状语从句的正常语序
questions.explain: "so + 形容词" 置于句首时，主句需部分倒装，即 "So profound was the impact..."，正常语序为 "The impact was so profound..."

questions.stem: It is the ability to adapt to changing circumstances, rather than sheer intelligence, that determines long-term success. 该句是什么句型？
opts: 强调句型，强调主语 the ability to adapt to changing circumstances
形式主语结构，It 作形式主语
定语从句，that 引导定语从句修饰 circumstances
主语从句，It 指代后面 that 从句的内容
questions.explain: 该句为 It is...that... 强调句型，去掉 It is...that... 后剩余部分仍为完整句子，强调主语 the ability to adapt to changing circumstances。

questions.stem: The theory, though widely accepted for decades, has recently been challenged by new empirical evidence that casts doubt on its core assumptions. 句中 "that casts doubt on its core assumptions" 修饰什么？
opts: 修饰 new empirical evidence，是定语从句
修饰 the theory，是同位语从句
修饰 decades，是定语从句
修饰 core assumptions，是宾语从句
questions.explain: that 引导的定语从句修饰先行词 new empirical evidence，that 在从句中作主语，指代 evidence。

questions.stem: Only by systematically analyzing the underlying data can researchers draw reliable conclusions. 该句的语法特点是什么？
opts: "Only + 状语" 置于句首，主句部分倒装
完全倒装，主语与谓语完全颠倒
省略 if 的虚拟条件句
正常语序的陈述句
questions.explain: "Only + 介词短语" 置于句首时，主句需部分倒装，将情态动词 can 提到主语 researchers 之前。

questions.stem: In the sentence "The idea that the function of government is to protect individual rights, which was championed by classical liberals, has profoundly shaped modern political thought," the grammatical function of the clause "that the function of government is to protect individual rights" is a(n) ______.
opts: attributive clause modifying 'the idea'
appositive clause explaining 'the idea'
subject clause serving as the main subject
adverbial clause of result
questions.explain: 考点：同位语从句与定语从句的区分。'that'引导的从句对抽象名词'the idea'进行内容解释，而非修饰限定，且'that'在从句中不作成分，故为同位语从句。

questions.stem: In the sentence "Were it not for the timely intervention of the central bank, the financial system would have collapsed entirely," the underlined part "Were it not for" expresses a ______.
opts: subjunctive condition contrary to present fact
subjunctive condition contrary to past fact
inverted conditional clause with implied 'if'
concessive clause meaning 'even if'
questions.explain: 考点：虚拟语气中的倒装结构。'Were it not for' = 'If it were not for'，是省略if的倒装虚拟条件句，表示与现在事实相反的假设。

questions.stem: In the sentence "The phenomenon, which has been extensively documented by sociologists over the past decade, illustrates how deeply ingrained social norms can influence individual behavior even in the absence of explicit enforcement," the clause "how deeply ingrained social norms can influence individual behavior even in the absence of explicit enforcement" functions as the ______.
opts: object clause of 'illustrates'
subject complement modifying 'the phenomenon'
attributive clause modifying 'social norms'
adverbial clause of manner
questions.explain: 考点：宾语从句的识别。'how'引导的从句作及物动词'illustrates'的宾语，说明'illustrates'的内容，是宾语从句。

questions.stem: In the sentence "Not until the early 20th century did physicists begin to grasp the profound implications of quantum mechanics, a theory that would ultimately challenge the very foundations of classical determinism," the phrase "a theory that would ultimately challenge the very foundations of classical determinism" is a(n) ______.
opts: appositive modifying 'quantum mechanics'
attributive clause modifying 'physicists'
adverbial clause of result
parenthetical element modifying the main verb
questions.explain: 考点：同位语结构。'a theory'是'quantum mechanics'的同位语，其后跟定语从句'that would...'进一步修饰该同位语，整体作补充说明。

questions.stem: In the sentence "The extent to which language shapes thought has been a subject of intense debate among linguists, psychologists, and philosophers alike," the subject of the sentence is ______.
opts: the extent
language
the extent to which language shapes thought
a subject of intense debate
questions.explain: 考点：主语识别与定语从句嵌套。'The extent to which language shapes thought'整体是名词短语作主语，其中'to which language shapes thought'是定语从句修饰'the extent'。

questions.stem: In the sentence "So pervasive has the influence of social media become that scholars have begun to speak of a new form of social organization, one that blurs the traditional boundary between public and private spheres," the structure "So pervasive has the influence of social media become that..." exemplifies ______.
opts: inversion caused by 'so...that' structure placed at the beginning
a subject-verb agreement error
an elliptical conditional sentence
a passive voice transformation
questions.explain: 考点：'so...that'结构引起的倒装。当'so+形容词/副词'置于句首时，主句需部分倒装，即'So pervasive has the influence...become that...'。

questions.stem: In the sentence "What distinguishes a truly great leader from a merely competent one is not only the ability to make sound decisions under pressure but also the capacity to inspire others to transcend their own limitations," the subject of the sentence is ______.
opts: a truly great leader
the ability to make sound decisions
What distinguishes a truly great leader from a merely competent one
the capacity to inspire others
questions.explain: 考点：主语从句。'What distinguishes...one'是'what'引导的主语从句，作整个句子的主语，谓语动词为'is'。

questions.stem: In the sentence "The researchers argue that, had the sample size been larger, the results would have reached statistical significance, thereby lending greater credibility to their hypothesis," the phrase "had the sample size been larger" is ______.
opts: a past perfect tense used for sequence of events
an inverted subjunctive condition referring to the past
a relative clause modifying 'the sample size'
a concessive clause meaning 'although the sample size was larger'
questions.explain: 考点：虚拟语气的倒装结构表过去条件。'had the sample size been larger' = 'if the sample size had been larger'，是省略if的倒装虚拟条件句，表示与过去事实相反的假设。

questions.stem: In the sentence "It is not so much the specific policies themselves as the underlying philosophy that defines the administration's approach to economic reform," the structure "not so much...as..." serves to ______.
opts: compare two equal elements in importance
emphasize the second element over the first
introduce a negation of both elements
indicate a cause-and-effect relationship
questions.explain: 考点：'not so much...as...'结构的含义。该结构意为'与其说……不如说……'，强调后者（the underlying philosophy）比前者（the specific policies themselves）更重要。

questions.stem: In the sentence "Only when we recognize that economic growth, however desirable, cannot be pursued at the expense of environmental sustainability can we begin to chart a truly viable path forward," the main clause is ______.
opts: Only when we recognize...
economic growth cannot be pursued
can we begin to chart a truly viable path forward
we recognize that economic growth...
questions.explain: 考点：'Only+状语'置于句首引起的倒装。主句为'can we begin to chart a truly viable path forward'，因'Only when...'置于句首，主句需部分倒装，将情态动词'can'提前至主语'we'之前。

questions.stem: In the passage, the author's use of the phrase 'a double-edged sword' primarily serves to:
opts: Introduce a new argument that contradicts the previous claim
Highlight the inherent ambiguity and potential risks of the discussed phenomenon
Provide a definitive solution to the problem outlined earlier
Summarize the positive aspects of the topic under discussion
questions.explain: 考点：修辞意图推断。'双刃剑'暗示事物兼具利弊两面，选项B准确捕捉了这种 ambiguity 和 risk 的修辞功能。

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the relationship between the first and second paragraphs of the text?
opts: The second paragraph provides empirical evidence that refutes the theoretical claim made in the first.
The second paragraph elaborates on a specific example to illustrate the general principle introduced in the first.
The second paragraph shifts to a completely unrelated topic, signaling a new line of inquiry.
The second paragraph restates the first paragraph's thesis in more accessible language.
questions.explain: 考点：段落逻辑关系识别。第二段通常通过具体例子展开第一段提出的抽象原则，选项B正确描述了'一般→具体'的递进关系。

questions.stem: The word 'ameliorate' in the context of the third paragraph most nearly means:
opts: Exacerbate
Mitigate
Obscure
Validate
questions.explain: 考点：上下文词义推断。'ameliorate'意为'改善、减轻'，与mitigate（缓解）语义最接近，而exacerbate（加剧）是反义干扰。

questions.stem: According to the passage, the primary reason why the author criticizes the conventional approach is that it:
opts: Overemphasizes quantitative data at the expense of qualitative insights
Fails to account for the historical context in which the phenomenon emerged
Relies on an outdated theoretical framework that has been empirically disproven
Ignores the interplay between individual agency and structural constraints
questions.explain: 考点：细节因果定位。原文批评传统方法忽视了个体能动性与结构约束之间的相互作用，选项D精准对应这一核心论点。

questions.stem: The author's tone in the concluding paragraph can best be described as:
opts: Cautiously optimistic
Bitterly ironic
Resignedly pessimistic
Detachedly analytical
questions.explain: 考点：语气态度推断。结论段通常呈现审慎乐观的态度，选项A'谨慎乐观'符合学术写作中既承认困难又展望可能的典型语气。

questions.stem: The function of the quotation from Smith (2019) in the fourth paragraph is to:
opts: Provide a counterargument that the author subsequently refutes
Lend authoritative support to the author's own thesis
Introduce a new perspective that diverges from the main argument
Offer a historical anecdote that enriches the narrative
questions.explain: 考点：引用功能分析。学术引用通常用于借助权威支持自身论点，选项B准确描述了引文作为论据支撑的功能。

questions.stem: Which of the following, if true, would most weaken the author's central argument?
opts: Recent studies show that the proposed solution has unintended negative consequences.
The historical examples cited by the author are found to be factually inaccurate.
A majority of experts in the field endorse the author's conclusions.
The data set used in the author's analysis is larger than those of previous studies.
questions.explain: 考点：论证削弱识别。如果解决方案产生意外负面后果，将直接削弱作者的核心论点，选项A构成最有效的反驳。

questions.stem: The passage mentions 'cognitive dissonance' primarily in order to:
opts: Introduce a psychological concept that explains the observed behavior
Dismiss the relevance of psychological factors in the analysis
Contrast it with a more recent theoretical development
Suggest that the phenomenon is purely psychological in nature
questions.explain: 考点：举例目的判断。引入'认知失调'这一心理学概念是为了解释前文描述的行为现象，选项A正确指出了其解释性功能。

questions.stem: Based on the passage, the author's attitude toward the current policy framework can be characterized as:
opts: Unqualified endorsement
Critical but constructive
Indifferent neutrality
Vehement opposition
questions.explain: 考点：作者态度辨析。作者既指出政策框架的不足又提出改进建议，选项B'批判但建设性'准确概括了这一辩证态度。

questions.stem: In the passage, the author's use of the phrase "a double-edged sword" (Paragraph 3) primarily serves to indicate that the technological innovation under discussion ______.
opts: A. brings both benefits and hidden risks that are equally significant
B. is as dangerous as it is beneficial, with no net positive effect
C. has been overhyped by the media and misunderstood by the public
D. cuts both ways in terms of economic impact but not social impact
questions.explain: 考点：修辞意图推断。"double-edged sword" 强调同一事物兼具利弊两面，且两方面都重要，A 准确概括了这种辩证关系。

questions.stem: According to the text, the author's attitude toward the proposed policy reform can best be described as ______.
opts: A. enthusiastic endorsement with minor reservations
B. cautious optimism tempered by practical concerns
C. outright opposition based on ideological grounds
D. detached neutrality with no personal stance
questions.explain: 考点：作者态度推断。拔高题要求区分 nuanced 态度，文中既有对改革潜力的肯定，又指出实施障碍，"cautious optimism" 最准确。

questions.stem: The word "anomaly" (Line 3, Paragraph 2) is closest in meaning to ______.
opts: A. a typical and recurring pattern
B. a deviation from the expected norm
C. an artificially induced phenomenon
D. a statistical outlier with no significance
questions.explain: 考点：上下文词义推断。"anomaly" 在学术语境中指偏离常规的异常现象，B 为最精确释义，干扰项利用常见误读设置。

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the logical structure of the passage?
opts: A. Problem identification → historical background → proposed solution → counterargument → conclusion
B. Thesis statement → supporting evidence → concession → refutation → reinforcement of thesis
C. Phenomenon description → causal analysis → comparative study → prediction → recommendation
D. Definition of concept → classification of types → exemplification → limitation → summary
questions.explain: 考点：篇章结构分析。拔高难度要求识别论证推进模式，B 对应经典议论文结构：立论—论证—让步—驳论—强化论点。

questions.stem: The author mentions the study by Thompson et al. (2019) primarily to ______.
opts: A. provide a definitive answer to the research question posed earlier
B. illustrate a counterintuitive finding that challenges the prevailing view
C. introduce a new methodology for measuring the discussed phenomenon
D. support a previously stated claim with empirical evidence
questions.explain: 考点：论据功能判断。拔高题要求区分引用目的，文中 Thompson 研究被用作支撑前文论点的实证依据，D 最符合论证逻辑。

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the last paragraph that the author believes the current approach to climate adaptation is ______.
opts: A. fundamentally sound but in need of minor adjustments
B. largely ineffective due to systemic structural flaws
C. too radical and likely to provoke public backlash
D. the best possible option given existing constraints
questions.explain: 考点：隐含观点推断。拔高题要求从字面信息推导深层判断，末段通过批评性措辞暗示现有方法存在根本性缺陷，B 正确。

questions.stem: The passage suggests that the main reason for the failure of the previous initiative was ______.
opts: A. insufficient funding and resource allocation
B. a lack of coordination among key stakeholders
C. the inherent contradiction in its design principles
D. external political interference at critical moments
questions.explain: 考点：因果逻辑定位。拔高题要求综合多处信息归因，文中明确指出失败源于设计原则的内在矛盾，C 为原文同义改写。

questions.stem: Which of the following statements, if true, would most seriously undermine the author's central argument?
opts: A. The data used in the study were collected from a non-representative sample
B. The historical precedent cited actually supports the opposite conclusion
C. The proposed solution has already been implemented successfully elsewhere
D. The author's definition of the key term differs from the academic consensus
questions.explain: 考点：论证削弱识别。拔高题要求评估证据对核心论证的威胁程度，样本偏差直接动摇论证基础，削弱力最强。

questions.stem: The tone of the passage can best be characterized as ______.
opts: A. scholarly and dispassionate, with an emphasis on objective analysis
B. urgent and alarmist, seeking to provoke immediate action
C. ironic and sarcastic, mocking opposing viewpoints
D. reflective and philosophical, exploring broader implications
questions.explain: 考点：语气判断。拔高题要求区分 subtle tonal cues，全文保持学术中立、客观分析的基调，A 准确概括。

questions.stem: The author implies that the conventional wisdom regarding urban sustainability is ______.
opts: A. largely correct but incomplete in its scope
B. fundamentally misguided and in need of revision
C. irrelevant to the challenges of developing countries
D. too theoretical to be practically applicable
questions.explain: 考点：隐含批判意图识别。拔高题要求捕捉作者对主流观点的否定态度，文中通过对比和反例暗示传统观点存在根本性错误，B 正确。

questions.stem: In the passage, the author's use of the phrase "intellectual scaffolding" (Paragraph 3) primarily serves to imply that theoretical frameworks are ________.
opts: temporary constructs subject to constant revision
rigid structures that resist empirical challenge
foundational supports that enable further knowledge building
ornamental additions with little practical value
questions.explain: 考点：修辞理解（metaphorical language）——‘scaffolding’比喻理论框架的支撑与奠基功能，而非临时性、僵化或装饰性。

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the relationship between the two experiments discussed in Paragraphs 2 and 4?
opts: The second experiment replicates the first under stricter conditions.
The second experiment challenges the first by introducing a confounding variable.
The second experiment extends the first by testing a different demographic.
The second experiment contradicts the first due to methodological flaws.
questions.explain: 考点：段落间逻辑关系——实验二通过改变被试群体（不同人口学特征）扩展了实验一的范围，而非简单复制或反驳。

questions.stem: The word "recalcitrant" (Line 3, Paragraph 5) most nearly means ________.
opts: stubbornly resistant to authority
unexpectedly cooperative under pressure
passively indifferent to external stimuli
actively hostile toward established norms
questions.explain: 考点：词汇推断（contextual vocabulary）——根据上下文‘recalcitrant data that refused to fit the model’，指数据顽固地不符合模型，即‘resistant’。

questions.stem: According to the passage, the mainstream view holds that economic recessions are primarily caused by ________.
opts: sudden drops in consumer confidence triggered by media panic
structural imbalances in supply and demand chains
exogenous shocks that disrupt financial equilibrium
cyclical fluctuations inherent in capitalist systems
questions.explain: 考点：细节定位与观点区分——文中明确主流经济学派将衰退归因于资本主义内在周期波动，而非外部冲击或信心危机。

questions.stem: The author mentions the case of the 18th-century maritime treaty (Paragraph 6) in order to ________.
opts: illustrate the failure of diplomatic negotiation in resolving territorial disputes
provide a historical precedent for the current geopolitical strategy
highlight the role of economic incentives in sustaining long-term agreements
criticize the short-sightedness of modern international policies
questions.explain: 考点：例证功能（example function）——该条约案例旨在证明经济利益激励对协议持久性的关键作用，呼应前文论点。

questions.stem: The primary purpose of the passage is to ________.
opts: compare two competing theories of language acquisition
advocate for a paradigm shift in neuroscience research methodology
critique the over-reliance on quantitative data in social sciences
reconcile contradictory findings from longitudinal and cross-sectional studies
questions.explain: 考点：主旨大意（main idea）——全文围绕社会科学中过度依赖量化数据的弊端展开批判，并呼吁方法多元化。

questions.stem: Which of the following, if true, would most weaken the author's argument in Paragraph 7?
opts: The sample size in the cited study was smaller than initially reported.
The correlation between variables disappeared when controlling for socioeconomic status.
The experimental results have been replicated in three independent laboratories.
The statistical model used was later found to contain a coding error.
questions.explain: 考点：论证削弱（weakening argument）——若控制社会经济地位后相关性消失，则表明原结论可能是虚假相关（spurious correlation），直接削弱因果主张。

questions.stem: The tone of the passage can best be described as ________.
opts: detached and clinical
skeptical and critical
enthusiastic and celebratory
ambivalent and equivocal
questions.explain: 考点：语气判断（authorial tone）——作者对主流观点持续提出质疑并用批判性措辞，整体语气为怀疑与批判。

questions.stem: Based on the passage, the author's attitude toward interdisciplinary research is one of ________.
opts: cautious endorsement tempered by methodological concerns
wholehearted advocacy without reservation
indifference regarding its practical applications
outright rejection as intellectually superficial
questions.explain: 考点：态度题（attitude）——作者虽支持跨学科研究，但反复强调方法整合中的风险，故为‘有保留的认可’。

questions.stem: In the passage, the author's use of the phrase 'a double-edged sword' primarily serves to emphasize that the technological advancement under discussion is:
opts: A. beneficial in all aspects and without any drawbacks
B. likely to cause more harm than good in the long run
C. capable of producing both positive and negative consequences simultaneously
D. a temporary phenomenon that will soon be replaced by newer innovations
questions.explain: 考点为修辞理解；'double-edged sword'是比喻，指同一事物兼具利弊两面，选项C准确概括了这种对立统一关系。

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the author's attitude toward the proposed economic reform as revealed in the text?
opts: A. Enthusiastic endorsement with no reservations
B. Cautious optimism tempered by practical concerns
C. Complete indifference to the potential outcomes
D. Veiled hostility masked by neutral language
questions.explain: 考点为态度推断；作者在文中既肯定改革前景又指出实施风险，'cautious optimism'准确匹配这种审慎积极的立场。

questions.stem: The word 'anomaly' in paragraph 3 most likely means:
opts: A. a typical and expected occurrence
B. something that deviates from the norm
C. a minor and insignificant detail
D. a deliberate and calculated action
questions.explain: 考点为词义推断；根据上下文逻辑，'anomaly'指与常规模式不符的异常现象，选项B符合该词在学术语境中的核心含义。

questions.stem: According to the passage, the primary reason why the researchers' initial hypothesis was rejected is that:
opts: A. the sample size was too small to draw any meaningful conclusions
B. subsequent data contradicted the predicted causal relationship
C. the funding agency withdrew support midway through the study
D. peer reviewers found the theoretical framework outdated
questions.explain: 考点为因果细节定位；文中明确说明后续数据与假设预测的因果关系相矛盾，这是假设被拒的直接原因。

questions.stem: The author mentions the historical precedent in paragraph 2 chiefly to:
opts: A. provide a comprehensive overview of all relevant past events
B. illustrate a recurring pattern that supports the current argument
C. criticize previous scholars for their methodological errors
D. suggest that history is irrelevant to contemporary analysis
questions.explain: 考点为例证功能分析；历史先例在论证中充当类比证据，用以揭示当前现象与历史模式之间的相似性，从而支持论点。

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that the government's policy shift was motivated primarily by:
opts: A. genuine concern for public welfare and social justice
B. pressure from international organizations and foreign investors
C. a desire to consolidate political power during an election year
D. internal bureaucratic conflicts within the administration
questions.explain: 考点为隐含信息推断；文中虽未明说，但通过选举年背景、政策时机与权力集中线索可推出政治动机是最合理解释。

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the cultural phenomenon described in the text is most strongly supported by the evidence presented?
opts: A. It is a completely unprecedented development in human history
B. Its roots can be traced to specific socioeconomic transformations
C. It has been universally embraced across all demographic groups
D. Its long-term effects are already fully understood by scholars
questions.explain: 考点为证据支持判断；文中通过数据与案例将现象与特定社会经济变迁建立因果链条，选项B有最充分的文本依据。

questions.stem: The author's argument in paragraph 4 relies on the assumption that:
opts: A. correlation between variables necessarily implies causation
B. the available data is both reliable and representative
C. alternative explanations have been completely ruled out
D. future trends will exactly mirror past patterns
questions.explain: 考点为隐含假设识别；论证有效性建立在数据可信与代表性前提之上，若此假设不成立则推理链条断裂。

questions.stem: The passage suggests that the mainstream interpretation of the event is problematic because it:
opts: A. overlooks crucial contextual factors that shaped the outcome
B. relies too heavily on quantitative rather than qualitative data
C. was developed by scholars with a clear ideological bias
D. fails to account for the role of individual agency
questions.explain: 考点为批判性阅读；作者指出主流解释的缺陷在于忽略关键语境因素，这导致对事件因果关系的片面理解。

questions.stem: The overall structure of the passage can best be described as:
opts: A. presenting a problem, analyzing its causes, and proposing a solution
B. comparing two competing theories and declaring a winner
C. tracing a chronological narrative from past to present
D. challenging a prevailing view and offering an alternative framework
questions.explain: 考点为篇章结构分析；全文以质疑主流观点开篇，逐步构建替代性解释框架，属于'立论-驳论'结构。

questions.stem: In the context of reading comprehension, the phrase 'the author's tone is predominantly one of' typically requires the reader to:
opts: Identify the main argument of the passage
Infer the author's attitude or emotional stance toward the subject
Summarize the supporting evidence used in the text
Determine the chronological order of events described
questions.explain: Tone questions test the reader's ability to infer the author's attitude (e.g., critical, supportive, neutral) from word choice and rhetorical devices, not merely to restate content.

questions.stem: When a passage states 'The findings, though groundbreaking, must be interpreted with caution,' the phrase 'must be interpreted with caution' primarily serves to:
opts: Undermine the credibility of the research entirely
Suggest that the findings are irrelevant to the discussion
Introduce a limitation or qualification to the preceding claim
Emphasize the absolute certainty of the results
questions.explain: Qualifying language (e.g., 'with caution') signals a limitation or caveat, a key skill in reading comprehension for discerning nuanced authorial stance.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the relationship between the first and second paragraphs in a typical argumentative passage?
opts: The second paragraph provides a counterexample that refutes the first paragraph's thesis
The second paragraph elaborates on or extends the idea introduced in the first paragraph
The second paragraph shifts to an entirely unrelated topic
The second paragraph repeats the first paragraph's content in different words
questions.explain: In well-structured argumentative texts, subsequent paragraphs typically develop, elaborate, or support the initial thesis rather than refute or repeat it.

questions.stem: The word 'ostensibly' in 'The policy was ostensibly designed to promote fairness' most likely indicates that the author believes:
opts: The policy was genuinely fair and effective
The stated purpose may not be the real purpose
The policy was implemented without any debate
The fairness of the policy is universally accepted
questions.explain: 'Ostensibly' signals a contrast between appearance and reality, a common lexical cue for detecting authorial skepticism or irony in reading passages.

questions.stem: In reading comprehension, an 'inference question' requires the reader to:
opts: Locate a fact explicitly stated in the passage
Paraphrase a sentence from the text
Draw a logical conclusion based on evidence in the text
Identify the grammatical structure of a complex sentence
questions.explain: Inference questions test the ability to read between the lines—combining textual evidence with logical reasoning to reach a conclusion not directly stated.

questions.stem: A passage that begins with a specific anecdote and then moves to a general discussion is using which rhetorical structure?
opts: Deductive reasoning (general to specific)
Inductive reasoning (specific to general)
Chronological narration (time order)
Compare-and-contrast organization
questions.explain: Inductive structure starts with concrete examples or anecdotes and builds toward a broader generalization, a common pattern tested in reading comprehension.

questions.stem: The phrase 'it is worth noting that' in a passage is most likely used to:
opts: Dismiss a point as unimportant
Introduce a digression unrelated to the main idea
Signal that the following information is particularly relevant or significant
Indicate uncertainty about the truth of the statement
questions.explain: Metadiscursive markers like 'it is worth noting that' guide reader attention, signaling emphasis and importance—a key cue for identifying main ideas.

questions.stem: When an author writes 'Critics argue that...' without immediately refuting the argument, the most likely purpose is to:
opts: Endorse the critics' position as the author's own
Present an opposing viewpoint before countering or contextualizing it
Suggest that the critics' argument is irrelevant
Conclude the passage with a neutral summary
questions.explain: Academic writing often uses concession structures—presenting opposing views ('Critics argue...') to later refute or qualify them, a common rhetorical pattern in reading passages.

questions.stem: In a passage discussing two competing theories, the phrase 'the latter' refers to:
opts: The first theory mentioned in the previous sentence
The second of two previously mentioned items
The theory that the author ultimately rejects
The theory that is supported by more evidence
questions.explain: Cohesive devices like 'the former' and 'the latter' are referencing tools; 'the latter' always refers to the second of two items just mentioned, essential for tracking reference in dense texts.

questions.stem: Which of the following is most likely to indicate that the author is about to present a conclusion?
opts: For example, ...
In contrast, ...
Thus, ...
Furthermore, ...
questions.explain: Conjunctive adverbs like 'thus,' 'therefore,' and 'consequently' signal logical conclusions or results, distinguishing them from exemplification ('for example'), contrast ('in contrast'), or addition ('furthermore').

questions.stem: In the passage, the author's use of the phrase 'a double-edged sword' primarily serves to indicate that the technology under discussion ________.
opts: has both beneficial and detrimental effects that are equally weighted
produces advantages that far outweigh its potential risks
is ultimately harmful despite its initial promise
creates effects that are difficult to predict or measure
questions.explain: 考点：修辞理解——'双刃剑'隐喻强调利弊共存且程度相当，干扰项常夸大一方或模糊化。

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the author's attitude toward the proposed reform in the text?
opts: Cautious optimism, acknowledging potential benefits while warning of implementation challenges
Unqualified endorsement, viewing the reform as an unequivocal solution to existing problems
Skeptical detachment, questioning the motives behind the reform without offering alternatives
Outright hostility, dismissing the reform as fundamentally flawed and counterproductive
questions.explain: 考点：态度题——作者态度常为审慎支持，干扰项将态度极端化（全盘肯定/全盘否定/冷漠）。

questions.stem: The author mentions 'the Hawthorne effect' in paragraph 3 primarily to ________.
opts: illustrate how observation itself can alter the behavior being studied
challenge the validity of the experimental results reported earlier
introduce a historical precedent that supports the main argument
contrast a well-known phenomenon with the less familiar one under discussion
questions.explain: 考点：例证功能——引用经典效应是为了类比说明'观察者效应'，干扰项常混淆支持/对比/质疑等逻辑关系。

questions.stem: According to the passage, the key factor distinguishing 'deep learning' from traditional machine learning is that deep learning ________.
opts: can automatically extract hierarchical features without manual engineering
requires significantly larger datasets to achieve comparable accuracy
operates on symbolic representations rather than numerical inputs
was developed exclusively for image recognition tasks
questions.explain: 考点：细节区分——深度学习核心优势是自动特征提取，干扰项混入数据量、符号主义等常见误解。

questions.stem: The word 'specious' (line 12, paragraph 2) most nearly means ________.
opts: plausible but false
immediately obvious
highly controversial
empirically verified
questions.explain: 考点：词汇推断——'specious'指外表诱人实则谬误，干扰项利用形近词或反义关系设置陷阱。

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the relationship between GDP growth and well-being is most consistent with the author's argument?
opts: Beyond a certain threshold, further GDP growth yields diminishing returns in subjective well-being
GDP growth and well-being are perfectly correlated across all income levels
Well-being is entirely determined by relative income rather than absolute income
GDP growth has no measurable impact on well-being in developed economies
questions.explain: 考点：观点归纳——作者常持'临界点后边际效益递减'的修正观点，干扰项将关系绝对化或完全否定。

questions.stem: The author structures the passage primarily by ________.
opts: presenting a prevailing view, then challenging it with counterevidence and offering a nuanced alternative
tracing a chronological narrative of how the phenomenon evolved over several decades
comparing and contrasting two competing theories without endorsing either one
defining a problem, analyzing its causes, and proposing a step-by-step solution
questions.explain: 考点：篇章结构——学术议论文典型结构是'立靶-批驳-提出新观点'，干扰项混淆时间顺序、对比或问题解决模式。

questions.stem: The author's argument in the final paragraph relies on the assumption that ________.
opts: the causal mechanisms identified in controlled experiments also operate in real-world settings
the statistical significance of the findings guarantees their practical importance
the sample population used in the study is representative of the global population
the historical trends observed will continue indefinitely into the future
questions.explain: 考点：假设识别——论证隐含'实验室结论可推广到现实'的假设，干扰项混淆统计显著性与实际意义、代表性或线性外推。

questions.stem: In the context of reading comprehension, the phrase 'the author's tone is predominantly ironic' suggests that the writer is most likely:
opts: A. expressing genuine admiration for the subject
B. conveying a meaning opposite to the literal words
C. providing a neutral and objective account
D. criticizing the subject in a straightforward manner
questions.explain: 考点：识别作者语气。反讽（ironic）的核心特征是字面意思与实际意图相反，故B正确。

questions.stem: When a passage states, 'The new policy, while hailed as a breakthrough, has been met with skepticism from those who remember similar promises,' the author's attitude toward the policy is best described as:
opts: A. wholehearted endorsement
B. cautious optimism
C. reserved skepticism
D. vehement opposition
questions.explain: 考点：推断作者态度。'hailed as a breakthrough'与'skepticism from those who remember'形成对比，暗示作者持保留质疑态度，故C正确。

questions.stem: In academic reading, the function of a 'hedging' expression (e.g., 'it is possible that,' 'may suggest') is primarily to:
opts: A. emphasize the certainty of the claim
B. introduce a counterargument
C. reduce the strength of the claim to avoid overgeneralization
D. signal a shift in topic
questions.explain: 考点：理解学术文本中的模糊限制语（hedging）。其功能是弱化断言力度、避免绝对化，故C正确。

questions.stem: Which of the following best illustrates the rhetorical device of 'analogy' in a persuasive text?
opts: A. 'The company's profits have fallen for three consecutive quarters.'
B. 'A government without transparency is like a ship without a compass.'
C. 'We must act now before it is too late.'
D. 'Studies show that 75% of participants agreed with the proposal.'
questions.explain: 考点：识别类比（analogy）修辞。B将政府比作船，属于类比；A为事实陈述，C为呼吁，D为数据引用。

questions.stem: When a reading passage contains the sentence, 'This argument, however, rests on a flawed premise,' the word 'however' signals a:
opts: A. continuation of the same line of reasoning
B. summary of the previous point
C. shift to a critical or contrasting perspective
D. reinforcement of the author's main thesis
questions.explain: 考点：理解语篇标记词（discourse marker）。'however'表示转折，引出与前文不同的批判性观点，故C正确。

questions.stem: In a complex academic text, the phrase 'it is not merely X, but rather Y' is used to:
opts: A. deny the existence of X entirely
B. elevate Y as a more important or accurate characterization than X
C. present X and Y as equally valid alternatives
D. introduce a chronological sequence
questions.explain: 考点：理解强调结构。'not merely...but rather'意在否定X的充分性，强调Y才是更准确的描述，故B正确。

questions.stem: When an author writes, 'Critics argue that the reform has failed; yet the data tell a different story,' the author is employing which rhetorical strategy?
opts: A. Straw man fallacy
B. Appeal to authority
C. Concession and refutation
D. Circular reasoning
questions.explain: 考点：识别让步-反驳策略。先承认批评观点（Critics argue...），再用'yet'引出反证（data tell a different story），故C正确。

questions.stem: The sentence 'The implications of this discovery are far-reaching, though its practical applications remain uncertain' contains a relationship of:
opts: A. cause and effect
B. contrast between significance and applicability
C. chronological progression
D. exemplification
questions.explain: 考点：理解句内逻辑关系。'far-reaching'与'uncertain'形成对比，强调意义重大但应用未明，故B正确。

questions.stem: In reading comprehension, an 'implicit assumption' underlying an argument is one that:
opts: A. is explicitly stated in the opening paragraph
B. is logically necessary for the argument to hold but not directly expressed
C. contradicts the main conclusion of the passage
D. is supported by empirical evidence cited in the text
questions.explain: 考点：理解隐含假设（implicit assumption）。它是论证成立所需但未明说的前提，故B正确。

questions.stem: When a passage uses the phrase 'to put it bluntly' before restating a point, the author's purpose is to:
opts: A. soften a controversial claim
B. introduce a tangential observation
C. present the idea in a more direct and unvarnished manner
D. signal a transition to a different topic
questions.explain: 考点：理解语用功能。'to put it bluntly'提示下文将以更直白、不加修饰的方式重述观点，故C正确。

questions.stem: In the context of reading comprehension, the phrase 'the author's tone can be inferred from the lexical choices' most directly suggests that:
opts: A. The author's emotional attitude is explicitly stated in the text.
B. Word selection serves as a key indicator of the writer's implicit stance.
C. Lexical density determines the overall readability of the passage.
D. Tone is irrelevant to the semantic interpretation of a text.
questions.explain: 考点：推断作者态度。题干指出语气可从词汇选择推断，选项B准确对应‘词汇选择是作者隐含立场的关键指标’，干扰项A错在‘explicitly stated’，C偷换概念为‘词汇密度’，D否定语气作用。

questions.stem: When a passage employs extensive use of concessive structures (e.g., 'although', 'nevertheless'), the primary rhetorical function is to:
opts: A. Introduce a series of unrelated examples.
B. Emphasize a contrast between an anticipated expectation and the actual claim.
C. Simplify the syntactic complexity for easier comprehension.
D. Provide chronological sequencing of events.
questions.explain: 考点：识别修辞功能。让步结构的核心功能是‘强调预期与实际情况的对比’，B准确；A、D偏离让步逻辑；C与事实相反（让步常增加复杂度）。

questions.stem: In advanced academic reading, the ability to distinguish between 'main idea' and 'supporting detail' is critical. Which of the following best characterizes a supporting detail?
opts: A. A broad generalization that encapsulates the author's central argument.
B. A specific piece of evidence, example, or statistic that bolsters the thesis.
C. A rhetorical question posed to engage the reader's curiosity.
D. A concluding remark that summarizes the entire passage.
questions.explain: 考点：区分主旨与细节。支持性细节是‘支撑论点的具体证据/例子/数据’，B正确；A是主旨；C是修辞手法；D是结论。

questions.stem: An author writes: 'The policy, though well-intentioned, ultimately exacerbated the very problem it sought to alleviate.' The word 'exacerbated' most likely means:
opts: A. Resolved completely.
B. Made worse or more severe.
C. Had no measurable impact.
D. Was partially effective.
questions.explain: 考点：上下文猜词义。‘exacerbated’在让步结构中与‘well-intentioned’形成对比，且与‘alleviate’反义，意为‘使恶化’，B正确。

questions.stem: Which of the following inference types is most characteristic of a 'critical reading' approach?
opts: A. Accepting the author's claims at face value without questioning.
B. Identifying underlying assumptions, biases, and logical gaps in the argument.
C. Memorizing factual information presented in the text.
D. Paraphrasing each sentence to ensure literal comprehension.
questions.explain: 考点：批判性阅读的本质。批判性阅读要求‘识别隐含假设、偏见和逻辑漏洞’，B正确；A是盲目接受；C、D停留在字面理解层面。

questions.stem: In a dense academic passage, the phrase 'this is not to say that...' typically signals:
opts: A. A direct contradiction of the previous statement.
B. A clarification or qualification to prevent misinterpretation.
C. An abrupt shift to an entirely new topic.
D. A summation of the author's final conclusion.
questions.explain: 考点：语篇标记功能。‘this is not to say that...’用于‘澄清或限定前文，防止误解’，B正确；A过于绝对；C、D不符合语用功能。

questions.stem: When evaluating the strength of an argument in a reading passage, which factor is LEAST relevant?
opts: A. The credibility and expertise of the sources cited.
B. The logical coherence between premises and conclusion.
C. The aesthetic appeal and stylistic elegance of the prose.
D. The presence of counterarguments and how they are addressed.
questions.explain: 考点：论证评估标准。论证强度取决于证据可信度(A)、逻辑连贯性(B)和反驳处理(D)；‘文笔优美’(C)与论证逻辑无关，是最不相关的因素。

questions.stem: An author uses the analogy 'Like a ship without a rudder, the new policy drifts aimlessly from one crisis to another.' The primary purpose of this analogy is to:
opts: A. Provide a literal description of maritime navigation.
B. Illustrate the lack of direction and coherent strategy in the policy.
C. Compare the policy's budget to the cost of a ship.
D. Suggest that the policy is sinking due to external pressures.
questions.explain: 考点：类比修辞的理解。类比将政策比作‘无舵之船’，核心意图是‘说明政策缺乏方向和连贯策略’，B正确；A拘泥字面；C、D无依据。

questions.stem: In advanced reading comprehension, the term 'coherence' refers to:
opts: A. The grammatical correctness of individual sentences.
B. The logical and conceptual unity that makes a text feel like a connected whole.
C. The use of sophisticated vocabulary to impress the reader.
D. The physical layout and formatting of the passage.
questions.explain: 考点：语篇连贯概念。连贯指‘逻辑和概念上的统一性，使文本成为有机整体’，B正确；A是语法正确性；C是词汇难度；D是排版。

questions.stem: A passage begins with a rhetorical question: 'Can we truly claim to have made progress when inequality persists?' This opening device is most effective for:
opts: A. Presenting a definitive answer immediately.
B. Engaging the reader and establishing the central problematic.
C. Summarizing the entire argument in one sentence.
D. Providing statistical evidence upfront.
questions.explain: 考点：开篇修辞问题的功能。修辞问题用于‘吸引读者并确立核心问题’，B正确；A与修辞问题性质矛盾；C、D不符合开篇策略。

questions.stem: In the passage, the author describes a phenomenon as 'a cognitive mirage' (Line 3, Paragraph 2). Which of the following best captures the implication of this phrase?
opts: It is a widely accepted truth that has been empirically verified.
It is an illusion created by flawed reasoning that appears convincing at first glance.
It is a rare mental disorder that affects only a small subset of the population.
It is a deliberate fabrication intended to mislead public opinion.
questions.explain: 考点：修辞性表达的理解——'cognitive mirage' 喻指看似合理实则谬误的认知幻觉，干扰项利用 'truth'、'disorder'、'fabrication' 制造迷惑。

questions.stem: The author mentions 'the Hawthorne effect' in Paragraph 3 primarily to
opts: illustrate how external observation can alter subjects' behavior, thereby confounding experimental results.
argue that all psychological experiments are inherently unreliable and should be abandoned.
praise the methodological rigor of early 20th-century industrial research.
suggest that workers' productivity is solely determined by lighting conditions.
questions.explain: 考点：例证功能——'Hawthorne effect' 是经典干扰变量案例，作者用它说明观察本身对行为的影响，干扰项过度概括或曲解原意。

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best reflects the author's attitude toward the 'replication crisis' in social psychology?
opts: It is an overblown concern that will naturally resolve with time.
It signals a fundamental flaw in the discipline's statistical practices and theoretical assumptions.
It is exclusively a problem of fraud and misconduct by a few researchers.
It has been completely solved by the adoption of preregistration and open data.
questions.explain: 考点：作者态度推断——'replication crisis' 指向系统性方法论问题，正确项强调统计实践与理论假设的缺陷，干扰项分别淡化、归因偏狭或过度乐观。

questions.stem: The phrase 'begging the question' in Paragraph 4 is used to describe an argument that
opts: raises an interesting new question for further investigation.
assumes the very point it is supposed to prove, creating a circular reasoning.
appeals to popular opinion as a substitute for logical evidence.
attacks the person making the argument rather than the argument itself.
questions.explain: 考点：逻辑谬误识别——'begging the question' 是循环论证，正确项准确描述其定义，干扰项分别为 'raising a question'、'appeal to popularity'、'ad hominem'。

questions.stem: According to the passage, the main weakness of the 'availability heuristic' in decision-making is that it
opts: relies on statistical base rates that are often outdated.
overweights vivid or recent examples while underweighting less memorable but more relevant data.
requires too much cognitive effort to be practically useful.
is only applicable to financial decisions, not to everyday judgments.
questions.explain: 考点：认知偏差机制——'availability heuristic' 依赖易得性（生动/近期信息）而非客观概率，正确项精准描述偏差方向，干扰项混淆其他启发式或限制适用范围。

questions.stem: The author's use of the term 'paradigm shift' (Paragraph 5) most closely aligns with which of the following?
opts: A gradual accumulation of minor adjustments within an existing framework.
A revolutionary transformation in foundational assumptions that redefines an entire field.
A temporary fad that gains popularity but soon fades without lasting impact.
A political maneuver by senior academics to maintain their institutional power.
questions.explain: 考点：学术术语理解——'paradigm shift' 是库恩提出的科学革命概念，指基本假设的根本性变革，干扰项混淆为渐进积累、短暂潮流或权力斗争。

questions.stem: In the context of the passage, the word 'equivocal' (Line 2, Paragraph 6) most nearly means
opts: unambiguous and clearly defined.
open to more than one interpretation; ambiguous.
ethically questionable or morally dubious.
statistically insignificant and therefore irrelevant.
questions.explain: 考点：上下文词义推测——'equivocal' 在学术语境中常表 '模棱两可'，正确项为同义替换，干扰项利用反义、道德联想和统计术语制造迷惑。

questions.stem: The author criticizes the 'file-drawer problem' primarily because it
opts: encourages researchers to publish only positive results, leading to a biased literature.
causes physical damage to laboratory equipment and data storage.
reduces the total number of academic journals available for publication.
is a bureaucratic hurdle that slows down the peer-review process.
questions.explain: 考点：研究方法论——'file-drawer problem' 指阴性结果被束之高阁导致发表偏倚，正确项点出选择性报告，干扰项均为字面或无关曲解。

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the author's view on 'statistical significance' as used in contemporary research?
opts: It is the sole and sufficient criterion for determining the truth of a hypothesis.
It has been widely misinterpreted and over-relied upon, often at the expense of effect size and practical relevance.
It is a useless concept that should be completely eliminated from scientific practice.
It is perfectly understood and correctly applied by the majority of researchers.
questions.explain: 考点：批判性推断——作者对 p 值滥用的批评是常见考点，正确项指出误解与过度依赖，干扰项分别为绝对化肯定、极端否定和盲目乐观。

questions.stem: The passage suggests that the 'Dunning-Kruger effect' is particularly problematic because it
opts: causes experts to underestimate their own abilities, leading to impostor syndrome.
creates a double burden: the unskilled lack both the competence and the metacognitive ability to recognize their incompetence.
is a rare phenomenon that only appears in laboratory settings with artificial tasks.
can be easily corrected by a single feedback session or training workshop.
questions.explain: 考点：经典效应理解——'Dunning-Kruger effect' 的核心是能力不足者元认知缺陷，正确项概括 '双重负担'，干扰项混淆为冒充者综合征、罕见性或易纠正。

questions.stem: In the sentence "That the brain, once thought to be fixed after childhood, can rewire itself in response to experience has been one of the most revolutionary discoveries in modern neuroscience," the grammatical function of the clause "That the brain ... experience" is:
opts: A. subject
B. object
C. appositive
D. adverbial
questions.explain: 主语从句（That引导的从句在整个句子中充当主语，谓语是has been）——识别名词性从句在长句中的主干位置是破解长难句的关键。

questions.stem: In "The idea that the mind, far from being a blank slate, is pre-equipped with a basic framework for acquiring language has been championed by linguists such as Noam Chomsky," the clause "that the mind ... language" functions as:
opts: A. subject clause
B. appositive clause
C. attributive clause
D. object clause
questions.explain: 同位语从句（that从句解释说明抽象名词idea，且从句成分完整，不是定语从句）——区分同位语从句与定语从句的关键是看that是否在从句中充当成分。

questions.stem: Which of the following sentences contains a non-restrictive attributive clause that modifies the entire preceding clause?
opts: A. The experiment failed, which surprised everyone in the lab.
B. The experiment which failed was conducted last month.
C. The professor who designed the experiment retired last year.
D. The data that were collected proved to be unreliable.
questions.explain: 非限制性定语从句which指代前面整个主句（实验失败这件事让所有人惊讶）——which指代整句时只能用非限制性定语从句，且不可用that替换。

questions.stem: In the sentence "Not until the 19th century, when the Industrial Revolution had already transformed Europe, did scientists begin to understand the true nature of heat," the grammatical structure used to emphasize time is:
opts: A. inverted structure after 'Not until' at the beginning
B. emphatic 'it is ... that' structure
C. a fronted adverbial clause without inversion
D. a passive voice construction
questions.explain: Not until置于句首引起主句部分倒装（did scientists begin）——否定词/短语位于句首时主谓部分倒装是长难句中的高频考点。

questions.stem: In "The phenomenon, whereby individuals in a group tend to conform to the majority opinion even when that opinion is clearly wrong, has been extensively studied by social psychologists," the word "whereby" functions to introduce a clause that is:
opts: A. attributive, modifying 'phenomenon'
B. adverbial, indicating manner
C. nominal, serving as subject
D. predicative, describing the subject
questions.explain: 关系副词whereby引导定语从句修饰先行词phenomenon（= by which phenomenon）——whereby在考研长难句中常引导定语从句，相当于by which/through which。

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly analyzes the structure of the sentence "What is particularly striking about the findings is that, despite decades of educational reform, the gap between rich and poor students has not narrowed"?
opts: A. Subject clause (What...findings) + linking verb + predicative clause (that...narrowed)
B. Attributive clause (What...findings) + main clause + object clause
C. Adverbial clause of concession + main clause + appositive clause
D. Main clause + attributive clause + adverbial clause of result
questions.explain: What引导主语从句作主语，is为系动词，that引导表语从句——主系表结构中嵌套名词性从句是考研长难句的典型模式。

questions.stem: In "The researchers argue that the mechanism by which the drug works is fundamentally different from what was previously assumed," the clause "by which the drug works" is:
opts: A. an attributive clause modifying 'mechanism'
B. an adverbial clause of manner
C. an object clause after 'argue'
D. a subject clause of the whole sentence
questions.explain: by which引导定语从句修饰mechanism（= the mechanism through which the drug works）——介词+关系代词引导定语从句是长难句中常见的复杂修饰结构。

questions.stem: The sentence "So pervasive are the effects of social media on young people's mental health that many governments have begun to consider regulatory measures" exemplifies:
opts: A. 'so...that' structure with partial inversion
B. a simple sentence with a compound predicate
C. a compound sentence with two independent clauses
D. a conditional sentence with implied 'if'
questions.explain: So+形容词置于句首引起主谓部分倒装（So pervasive are...that...）——so/such...that结构中的so位于句首时主句需倒装，是考研语法拔高题的重点。

questions.stem: In "Had it not been for the timely intervention of the central bank, the financial system would have collapsed entirely," the underlined part "Had it not been for" expresses:
opts: A. a past unreal condition (subjunctive mood)
B. a present factual condition
C. a future possible condition
D. a concession meaning 'even if'
questions.explain: Had it not been for = If it had not been for，表示与过去事实相反的虚拟条件句——省略if的倒装虚拟条件是长难句中的高级语法现象。

questions.stem: Which of the following sentences contains a dangling modifier that creates ambiguity?
opts: A. Walking through the museum, the ancient artifacts caught my attention.
B. Walking through the museum, I was captivated by the ancient artifacts.
C. While I was walking through the museum, the ancient artifacts caught my attention.
D. The ancient artifacts, as I walked through the museum, caught my attention.
questions.explain: 垂悬分词（Walking的逻辑主语与主句主语the ancient artifacts不一致）——分词作状语时其逻辑主语必须等于主句主语，否则构成垂悬修饰错误，是长难句语法纠错题的高频考点。

questions.stem: The phenomenon that the more we consume, the more we seem to want, which economists have long dismissed as irrational, may actually have deep evolutionary roots that predate modern capitalism.
opts: 主语从句
同位语从句
定语从句
表语从句
questions.explain: that引导的从句紧跟在抽象名词phenomenon后，说明其具体内容，不作成分，为同位语从句。

questions.stem: That the brain can rewire itself in response to experience, a concept known as neuroplasticity, has been one of the most revolutionary discoveries in modern neuroscience, overturning centuries of dogma.
opts: 主语从句
宾语从句
定语从句
状语从句
questions.explain: That引导的从句位于句首作主语，谓语为has been，是典型的主语从句结构。

questions.stem: What distinguishes the truly creative mind from the merely competent one is not the absence of failure, but the capacity to transform each setback into a stepping stone toward a more refined vision.
opts: 主语从句
表语从句
宾语从句
同位语从句
questions.explain: What引导的从句位于句首作主语，谓语为is，是主语从句，what在从句中作主语。

questions.stem: The hypothesis that language shapes thought, which has been hotly debated since Whorf first proposed it, finds new support in a series of experiments conducted on bilingual speakers.
opts: that引导同位语从句，which引导非限制性定语从句
that引导定语从句，which引导非限制性定语从句
that引导同位语从句，which引导限制性定语从句
that引导主语从句，which引导状语从句
questions.explain: that从句说明hypothesis内容，为同位语从句；which从句修饰先行词hypothesis，为非限制性定语从句。

questions.stem: It is not so much that social media has changed how we communicate, but rather that it has fundamentally altered the very structure of attention, a faculty upon which all higher cognition depends.
opts: 主语从句
表语从句
宾语从句
同位语从句
questions.explain: It is not so much that... but rather that... 结构中，that从句位于系动词is之后作表语，为表语从句。

questions.stem: The extent to which an individual's success depends on factors beyond their control, such as family background and geographic luck, is far greater than most meritocratic narratives are willing to acknowledge.
opts: to which引导定语从句，修饰extent
to which引导宾语从句，修饰depends
to which引导状语从句，修饰greater
to which引导主语从句，修饰factors
questions.explain: to which引导定语从句修饰先行词extent，相当于the extent that an individual's success depends on...

questions.stem: Whether a society can sustain long-term economic growth while simultaneously reducing inequality is a question that has divided economists for decades, with no consensus in sight.
opts: 主语从句
表语从句
宾语从句
定语从句
questions.explain: Whether引导的从句位于句首作主语，谓语为is，为主语从句。

questions.stem: The assumption underlying most economic models — that individuals act rationally in their own self-interest — has come under increasing scrutiny from behavioral economists, who argue that humans are far more susceptible to cognitive biases than traditional theory allows.
opts: 破折号内that从句为同位语从句，解释assumption
破折号内that从句为定语从句，修饰individuals
破折号内that从句为宾语从句，作act的宾语
破折号内that从句为表语从句，位于系动词后
questions.explain: that从句位于抽象名词assumption后，用破折号隔开，说明其具体内容，为同位语从句。

questions.stem: Not until the late 20th century did historians begin to recognize that the lived experiences of ordinary people, rather than the decisions of elites, constitute the true fabric of historical change.
opts: 倒装结构 + that引导宾语从句
倒装结构 + that引导定语从句
正常语序 + that引导表语从句
正常语序 + that引导主语从句
questions.explain: Not until置于句首引起部分倒装，did historians begin...；that从句作recognize的宾语，为宾语从句。

questions.stem: So pervasive is the influence of algorithmic recommendation systems that it is no exaggeration to say they have become the primary architects of public opinion in the digital age.
opts: so...that...结构，主句倒装，that引导结果状语从句
so...that...结构，主句倒装，that引导定语从句
so...that...结构，主句正常，that引导同位语从句
so...that...结构，主句倒装，that引导主语从句
questions.explain: So pervasive置于句首引起主谓倒装，that引导结果状语从句，构成so...that...结构，表'如此……以至于……'。

questions.stem: In the sentence "That the brain, once thought to be fixed and immutable after childhood, can continue to change and adapt throughout life has been one of the most exciting discoveries in neuroscience.", the subject of the main clause is:
opts: the brain
That the brain...throughout life
one of the most exciting discoveries
the brain, once thought to be fixed and immutable after childhood
questions.explain: 考点：名词性从句作主语。整个"That...throughout life"是主语从句，谓语是has been，不能误将从句内部的主语the brain当作主句主语。

questions.stem: In "Not until the 1980s did economists begin to fully appreciate the complexity of global financial systems.", the inverted structure is used because:
opts: the sentence is a question
