D. 直接结束，无任何总结
questions.explain: 好的结尾应简要总结前文要点，并适当升华（如展望、建议），而非机械重复或引入新内容。

questions.stem: 写作中，句子多样性（sentence variety）指的是？
opts: A. 每句话长度完全相同
B. 交替使用简单句、并列句和复合句
C. 全部使用疑问句
D. 只使用一种句型以保持统一
questions.explain: 句子多样性指灵活运用不同句式（简单句、并列句、复合句），使文章节奏有变化、表达更丰富。

questions.stem: 在考研英语写作评分标准中，"Coherence and Cohesion"（连贯与衔接）主要考察的是？
opts: A. 单词拼写是否正确
B. 句子之间和段落之间是否逻辑通顺、衔接自然
C. 语法是否完全没有错误
D. 字数是否达到要求
questions.explain: 连贯与衔接考察的是文章的逻辑流畅度和衔接手段的使用，是评分的重要维度之一。

questions.stem: 在英语写作中，下列哪个连接词最适合表示“因果”关系？
opts: However
Therefore
Moreover
Meanwhile
questions.explain: Therefore 表示“因此”，用于引出结果或结论，是表示因果关系的典型连接词。

questions.stem: 写议论文时，表达“我认为”最正式、最推荐使用的短语是？
opts: I think
In my opinion
I guess
As far as I'm concerned
questions.explain: In my opinion 是议论文中表达个人观点最常用且得体的正式表达。

questions.stem: 下列哪个句子在英语写作中属于典型的“主题句”（topic sentence）？
opts: I like reading books.
There are three main reasons why exercise is important.
She went to the store yesterday.
The cat is sleeping on the sofa.
questions.explain: 主题句应概括段落主旨，选项 B 明确点明“运动重要的三个原因”，符合主题句特征。

questions.stem: 在英语写作中，下列哪组词属于“正式学术词汇”，适合用于论文写作？
opts: kids / a lot / good
children / numerous / beneficial
guys / tons of / nice
folks / loads of / great
questions.explain: children, numerous, beneficial 均为正式学术词汇，适合用于论文或正式写作中。

questions.stem: 写作中为避免重复，用下列哪个词替换“important”最恰当？
opts: big
crucial
nice
fun
questions.explain: crucial 与 important 同义且更正式，是写作中替换 important 的常用高级词汇。

questions.stem: 在英语写作中，下列哪个标点符号不能用于连接两个完整的句子？
opts: 分号 (;)
逗号 (,)
句号 (.)
连词 + 逗号 (and,)
questions.explain: 逗号不能直接连接两个独立分句，否则构成逗号拼接错误（comma splice）。

questions.stem: 写英语作文结尾段时，下列哪个短语最适合用于“总结全文”？
opts: First of all
In conclusion
For example
On the other hand
questions.explain: In conclusion 是结尾段总结全文最常用、最标准的过渡短语。

questions.stem: 下列哪个句子存在“悬垂修饰语”（dangling modifier）错误？
opts: Walking to school, the sun rose.
Walking to school, I saw the sun rise.
After finishing homework, she went to bed.
Having eaten lunch, he continued working.
questions.explain: Walking to school 的逻辑主语应与主句主语一致，但 the sun 不能走路，造成悬垂修饰语错误。

questions.stem: 在英语写作中，下列哪个词属于“过渡词”且表示“对比”关系？
opts: Furthermore
In addition
However
Therefore
questions.explain: However 表示转折对比，是写作中引出相反观点的常用过渡词。

questions.stem: 写英语作文时，下列哪种做法最有助于提升文章的“连贯性”（coherence）？
opts: 每句都用不同的主语
大量使用生僻词汇
合理使用过渡词和指代
尽可能写长句
questions.explain: 合理使用过渡词和指代（如 this, it, they）能有效增强段落间的逻辑衔接与连贯性。

questions.stem: 在英语议论文写作中，表达“在我看来”最正式、最常用的短语是？
opts: A. I think
B. In my opinion
C. I guess
D. As for me
questions.explain: In my opinion 是学术写作中表达个人观点的标准正式短语，比 I think 更正式，比 I guess 更确定，比 As for me 更规范。

questions.stem: 以下哪个连接词最适合用于引出“相反”的观点？
opts: A. Moreover
B. In addition
C. On the contrary
D. Therefore
questions.explain: On the contrary 用于引出与前文相反的观点；Moreover 和 In addition 表递进，Therefore 表结果。

questions.stem: 写作中“First and foremost”常用于什么位置？
opts: A. 结尾段
B. 开头引出第一个论点
C. 举例之后
D. 让步转折时
questions.explain: First and foremost 是引出第一个论点或首要理由的常用短语，通常出现在主体段开头。

questions.stem: 以下哪个句子在英语写作中属于“主题句”（topic sentence）？
opts: A. There are many reasons for this phenomenon.
B. The first reason is that technology improves efficiency.
C. In conclusion, we should take action.
D. For example, smartphones are widely used.
questions.explain: 主题句概括段落的中心论点，B 明确提出了第一个原因，是典型主题句；A 是引出句，C 是结论句，D 是举例句。

questions.stem: 写作中“Last but not least”的正确用法是？
opts: A. 用于开头段引出背景
B. 用于结尾段总结全文
C. 用于主体段引出最后一个论点
D. 用于举例之后补充说明
questions.explain: Last but not least 用于主体段中引出最后一个论点或理由，表示虽然最后但同样重要。

questions.stem: 以下哪个短语最适合用于“举例说明”？
opts: A. In other words
B. For instance
C. As a result
D. In contrast
questions.explain: For instance 是引出具体例子的标准短语；In other words 表换种说法，As a result 表结果，In contrast 表对比。

questions.stem: 英语作文结尾段中，以下哪个表达最合适？
opts: A. All in all, I think it is good.
B. To sum up, the benefits outweigh the drawbacks.
C. That's my opinion.
D. So this is the end.
questions.explain: To sum up 是正式结尾段的常用总结短语，搭配完整观点表述，比口语化的 A/C/D 更符合学术写作规范。

questions.stem: 写作中“It is widely acknowledged that...”的作用是？
opts: A. 表达个人猜测
B. 引出公认事实或普遍观点
C. 提出反对意见
D. 给出具体数据
questions.explain: It is widely acknowledged that... 用于引出被广泛认可的事实或观点，增强论证的客观性和说服力。

questions.stem: 以下哪个词不属于“因果”关系连接词？
opts: A. Therefore
B. Consequently
C. Nevertheless
D. Hence
questions.explain: Nevertheless 表转折让步，意为“然而、尽管如此”；Therefore、Consequently、Hence 均表因果关系。

questions.stem: 在英语写作中，以下哪种做法最有助于提升文章的“连贯性”（coherence）？
opts: A. 每句都用简单句
B. 大量使用高级词汇
C. 合理使用过渡词和指代
D. 每段只写一句话
questions.explain: 合理使用过渡词（如 however, therefore）和指代（如 this, these）能有效连接前后文，是提升连贯性的核心手段。

questions.stem: 在英语写作中，下列哪一项是段落主题句（topic sentence）最常出现的位置？
opts: A. 段落末尾
B. 段落中间
C. 段落开头
D. 段落的任何位置均可，无固定规律
questions.explain: 英语议论文段落通常以主题句开头（段首），便于读者快速把握段落主旨，这是最经典、最常用的写法。

questions.stem: 写作中，下列哪一项是“议论文（argumentative essay）”最核心的要素？
opts: A. 生动的描写
B. 明确的论点与有力的论据
C. 华丽的辞藻
D. 完整的时间线
questions.explain: 议论文的核心在于提出明确的论点（thesis）并用充分的论据（evidence）进行论证，而非单纯追求语言华丽或叙事完整。

questions.stem: 在英语写作中，使用“Firstly, Secondly, Finally”这类连接词的主要作用是？
opts: A. 增加字数
B. 使文章押韵
C. 体现逻辑层次与连贯性
D. 替换主语
questions.explain: 过渡词（transition words）如Firstly/Secondly/Finally能清晰展示论述顺序，增强文章的连贯性与逻辑性。

questions.stem: 下列哪一项是英语写作中“避免重复”的有效手段？
opts: A. 每句都用同一个主语
B. 使用同义词或代词替换
C. 删除所有修饰语
D. 将句子全部写成简单句
questions.explain: 使用同义词（synonyms）或代词（pronouns）替换前文已出现的词语，是避免重复、提升语言多样性的常用技巧。

questions.stem: 在英语写作中，一篇标准的“五段式作文”通常包含哪几个部分？
opts: A. 引言段、三个主体段、结论段
B. 引言段、两个主体段、结论段
C. 五个主体段
D. 引言段、一个主体段、结论段
questions.explain: 五段式作文（five-paragraph essay）的标准结构为：1个引言段（introduction）+ 3个主体段（body paragraphs）+ 1个结论段（conclusion）。

questions.stem: 写作中，下列哪一项是“论据（evidence）”的正确示例？
opts: A. “我认为空气污染很严重。”
B. “根据世界卫生组织2023年报告，全球90%的人口呼吸着污染空气。”
C. “空气污染不好。”
D. “也许空气污染是个问题。”
questions.explain: 论据需要具体、可验证的事实或数据支撑，选项B引用了权威报告和具体数据，是有效的论据；其余选项为主观判断或模糊表述。

questions.stem: 在英语写作中，下列哪一项属于“正式学术写作”应避免的语言？
opts: A. 精确的数据引用
B. 客观的第三人称
C. 缩略形式如“don't”“can't”
D. 严谨的逻辑连接词
questions.explain: 正式学术写作要求使用完整形式（do not / cannot），避免缩略形式（contractions），以保持语体的正式与严谨。

questions.stem: 写作中，下列哪一项是“结论段（conclusion）”的主要功能？
opts: A. 提出全新的论点
B. 重复全文每一句话
C. 总结主要观点并重申中心论点
D. 列出所有参考文献
questions.explain: 结论段应总结正文的主要观点并重申中心论点（thesis restatement），而非引入新论点或简单重复全文。

questions.stem: 在英语写作中，“The chart illustrates that...”这种句型属于哪种写作功能？
opts: A. 表达个人情感
B. 描述图表数据
C. 提出反对观点
D. 给出建议
questions.explain: “The chart illustrates that...”是典型的图表描述句型，常用于雅思小作文或数据类写作中，用于客观呈现图表信息。

questions.stem: 下列哪一项是提升英语写作“连贯性（coherence）”的最佳做法？
opts: A. 每个句子都独立成段
B. 大量使用生僻词汇
C. 合理使用代词、过渡词和逻辑连接词
D. 只写短句，避免任何连接
questions.explain: 连贯性依赖代词指代、过渡词和逻辑连接词等衔接手段（cohesive devices），使句子之间逻辑流畅、关系清晰。

questions.stem: 在考研英语大作文中，第一段通常被称为：
opts: 主体段
结论段
描述段（图表/图画描述）
过渡段
questions.explain: 考研英语大作文第一段要求描述图表或图画内容，故称描述段。

questions.stem: 以下哪个连接词最适合用于表示因果关系的段落衔接？
opts: However
Therefore
Moreover
Meanwhile
questions.explain: Therefore 表示“因此”，是典型的因果连接词，用于引出结果。

questions.stem: 写议论文时，提出反面观点后常用哪个词来转折并重申己方立场？
opts: Furthermore
In addition
Nevertheless
For example
questions.explain: Nevertheless 表示“然而”，用于转折后重申观点，符合议论文反驳逻辑。

questions.stem: 以下哪个句型更适合用于考研作文的结尾段？
opts: As is shown in the picture...
Only in this way can we...
There is a heated debate about...
The chart illustrates that...
questions.explain: Only in this way can we... 是倒装强调句型，常用于结尾段提出建议或展望。

questions.stem: 在英语写作中，避免重复使用同一词汇的最佳策略是：
opts: 全部使用简单词
使用同义替换（paraphrase）
每句都用不同句式
尽量少写内容
questions.explain: 同义替换是写作中避免重复、提升词汇多样性的核心技巧。

questions.stem: 以下哪个选项属于“高分句型”中的倒装结构？
opts: I think that...
Not only does it bring benefits, but also...
It is important that...
There are many reasons...
questions.explain: Not only 置于句首引起部分倒装，是典型的高分倒装句型。

questions.stem: 考研英语大作文第二段（主体段）的核心功能是：
opts: 描述数据变化
分析原因或展开论证
重复第一段内容
给出个人联系方式
questions.explain: 第二段要求对图画/图表所反映的现象进行分析或论证，是文章核心。

questions.stem: 以下哪个词或短语不适合用于作文开头引出话题？
opts: Recently, the issue of... has aroused public concern.
As is vividly depicted in the cartoon...
In conclusion, I firmly believe that...
It is universally acknowledged that...
questions.explain: In conclusion 是结尾段标志词，不能用于开头引出话题。

questions.stem: 写作中，为了使段落内部逻辑连贯，应使用：
opts: 随机词汇
过渡词与衔接手段（cohesive devices）
长难句堆砌
全部使用被动语态
questions.explain: 过渡词与衔接手段能确保段落内句子之间逻辑流畅、语义连贯。

questions.stem: 在考研英语写作评分标准中，“语法多样性”指的是：
opts: 只用简单句
正确使用多种句子结构（复合句、从句等）
每句都写20个词以上
避免使用任何连词
questions.explain: 语法多样性指灵活运用简单句、并列句、复合句等多种结构，而非单一重复。

questions.stem: 在英语写作中，以下哪个连接词最适合表示“因果关系”？
opts: However
Therefore
Moreover
Nevertheless
questions.explain: Therefore 表示“因此”，是典型的因果连接词；However 表转折，Moreover 表递进，Nevertheless 表让步。

questions.stem: 写作中，下列哪个短语用于引出“对比”关系最为恰当？
opts: In addition
On the contrary
As a result
For example
questions.explain: On the contrary 表示“相反”，用于引出对比；In addition 表递进，As a result 表因果，For example 表举例。

questions.stem: 在议论文写作中，表达“我认为”最正式且推荐使用的短语是？
opts: I think
I guess
From my perspective
I suppose
questions.explain: From my perspective 是正式写作中表达个人观点的地道短语，比 I think / I guess / I suppose 更学术化。

questions.stem: 以下哪个句子在学术写作中属于“主题句”（topic sentence）？
opts: There are many reasons.
First of all, technology has changed our daily life.
I will talk about this.
It is a good thing.
questions.explain: 主题句应明确概括段落中心思想，“First of all, technology has changed our daily life” 清晰点明段落主旨。

questions.stem: 写作中，下列哪个词可以替换“good”以提升词汇多样性？
opts: Nice
Beneficial
Fine
Okay
questions.explain: Beneficial（有益的）是比 good 更正式、更具学术感的替换词，适合写作场景；nice/fine/okay 过于口语化。

questions.stem: 英语写作中，段落之间实现“连贯性”最常用的手段是？
opts: 使用短句
使用过渡词
使用被动语态
使用复杂词汇
questions.explain: 过渡词（如 however, therefore, moreover）是连接段落、实现连贯性的核心手段。

questions.stem: 以下哪个句子在写作中属于“具体论据”而非“笼统陈述”？
opts: Many people like it.
It is very important.
A 2023 survey shows that 70% of students prefer online learning.
There are some advantages.
questions.explain: 具体论据应包含数据、事实或引用，“A 2023 survey shows that 70%...” 提供了具体数据，属于有力论据。

questions.stem: 在英语写作结尾段中，以下哪个表达最适合“总结全文”？
opts: In conclusion
By the way
To begin with
For instance
questions.explain: In conclusion 是标准的结尾总结用语；By the way 表示附带提及，To begin with 用于开头，For instance 用于举例。

questions.stem: 写作中，下列哪项属于“避免中式英语”的有效策略？
opts: 逐字翻译中文句子
直接使用中文标点
多用英语固定搭配和句型
尽量使用长难句
questions.explain: 多用英语固定搭配和地道句型可以有效避免中式英语；逐字翻译和直接使用中文标点都是常见错误。

questions.stem: 在考研英语写作中，以下哪个评分标准最为关键？
opts: 拼写完全正确
字数越多越好
内容切题、逻辑清晰、语言准确
使用最复杂的词汇
questions.explain: 考研写作评分核心是内容切题、逻辑清晰、语言准确；单纯拼写、字数或复杂词汇都不是决定性因素。

questions.stem: In the context of reading comprehension, which of the following best describes the function of a 'topic sentence' in an academic paragraph?
opts: It provides a detailed example to support the main argument.
It introduces the central idea that the rest of the paragraph develops.
It summarizes the entire passage in a single concise statement.
It transitions the reader from one paragraph to the next.
questions.explain: A topic sentence states the main idea of the paragraph, which is then elaborated by supporting sentences.

questions.stem: When an author uses the phrase 'on the other hand' in an argumentative passage, the primary rhetorical function is to:
opts: Introduce a completely unrelated topic.
Signal a shift to a contrasting perspective.
Emphasize the previous point by restating it.
Provide a chronological sequence of events.
questions.explain: The phrase 'on the other hand' is a discourse marker that signals a contrast or opposing viewpoint.

questions.stem: Which of the following inferences is most strongly supported by the statement: 'The experiment's results were statistically significant, yet the sample size was notably small'?
opts: The small sample size invalidates the statistical significance entirely.
The author believes the results are definitive and beyond question.
The author implies a note of caution despite the significant findings.
The experiment was conducted with perfect methodological rigor.
questions.explain: The word 'yet' signals a concession, suggesting that while results are significant, the small sample size warrants caution in interpretation.

questions.stem: In reading comprehension, the term 'author's tone' primarily refers to:
opts: The literal meaning of the words used in the passage.
The emotional attitude or stance conveyed through word choice and style.
The grammatical complexity of the sentences employed.
The historical context in which the text was written.
questions.explain: Tone reflects the author's attitude (e.g., critical, optimistic, skeptical) as expressed through diction and rhetorical devices.

questions.stem: When a passage states that 'the correlation between A and B is not necessarily causal,' the author is most likely cautioning against:
opts: Confusing coincidence with causation.
Overlooking the statistical significance of the data.
Assuming that A and B are completely unrelated.
Ignoring the possibility of a third variable.
questions.explain: The phrase 'not necessarily causal' warns against the logical fallacy of assuming correlation implies causation.

questions.stem: Which of the following best illustrates the reading skill of 'making an inference'?
opts: Identifying the dictionary definition of an unfamiliar word.
Counting the number of supporting details in a paragraph.
Drawing a logical conclusion based on evidence in the text.
Paraphrasing the first sentence of each paragraph.
questions.explain: Inference involves reading between the lines—using textual evidence to arrive at a conclusion not explicitly stated.

questions.stem: In a dense academic passage, the phrase 'it is worth noting that' serves to:
opts: Dismiss the following information as unimportant.
Highlight a point the author considers particularly significant.
Indicate that the author is uncertain about the claim.
Signal the end of the argument and the beginning of a summary.
questions.explain: The phrase 'it is worth noting that' is a metadiscursive cue used to draw the reader's attention to a key point.

questions.stem: When an author juxtaposes two contrasting theories in a passage, the likely purpose is to:
opts: Prove that one theory is completely false and the other is true.
Avoid taking a clear stance on the issue being discussed.
Highlight differences and possibly evaluate their relative merits.
Confuse the reader by presenting contradictory information.
questions.explain: Juxtaposition of contrasting theories is a rhetorical strategy to clarify distinctions and enable critical evaluation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most reliable indicator that a word or phrase is being used in a figurative, rather than literal, sense?
opts: The word appears in a dictionary with multiple definitions.
The literal interpretation would result in a logical contradiction or absurdity.
The word is placed at the beginning of a sentence.
The word is a noun rather than a verb.
questions.explain: Figurative language often creates a semantic clash with the surrounding context, making a literal reading impossible or nonsensical.

questions.stem: In critical reading, the term 'unstated assumption' refers to:
opts: A fact that is explicitly proven with data in the passage.
An idea that the author takes for granted without explicitly stating it.
A conclusion that the reader is forced to accept without evidence.
A rhetorical question posed by the author to engage the audience.
questions.explain: An unstated assumption is a premise that is not directly expressed but is necessary for the author's argument to hold logically.

questions.stem: In the context of reading comprehension, the phrase "the author's tone" most accurately refers to:
opts: The literal meaning of the words used in the passage
The emotional attitude or stance conveyed by the writer toward the subject
The grammatical structure and sentence complexity of the text
The chronological order in which events are presented
questions.explain: 考点：作者语气（tone）是阅读中理解作者立场与情感倾向的关键，需通过用词、修辞和语境推断，而非字面或结构信息。

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the function of a "transitional paragraph" in an academic passage?
opts: It introduces a completely new topic unrelated to the previous discussion
It summarizes the entire passage in a single paragraph
It bridges two sections by showing logical connections between ideas
It provides statistical data to support the author's main argument
questions.explain: 考点：过渡段的功能是衔接前后文、展示逻辑关系，帮助读者理解论证脉络，属于篇章结构理解的核心能力。

questions.stem: When an author uses the rhetorical device of "understatement" in a passage, the intended effect is most likely to:
opts: Exaggerate the importance of a point to persuade the reader
Present a fact in a deliberately restrained way to create irony or emphasis
Provide multiple examples to clarify a complex concept
Use technical jargon to establish credibility with experts
questions.explain: 考点：低调陈述（understatement）通过故意弱化表达来产生反讽或强调效果，是阅读理解中识别修辞意图的重要考点。

questions.stem: In reading comprehension, the term "inference" refers to:
opts: A fact explicitly stated in the first sentence of a paragraph
A conclusion drawn from evidence and reasoning rather than from explicit statements
A direct quotation from an authoritative source
A statistical generalization based on numerical data in the text
questions.explain: 考点：推断（inference）是阅读理解中超越字面信息、基于文本线索和逻辑推理得出隐含意义的能力，与直接信息区分是高频考点。

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most reliable indicator that a sentence contains the main idea of a paragraph?
opts: It appears at the end of the paragraph with a summarizing transition
It contains a proper noun or a technical term
It is the longest sentence in the paragraph
It is written in passive voice to emphasize objectivity
questions.explain: 考点：段落主旨句常出现在段首或段尾，并伴有总结性过渡词（如 therefore, in conclusion），而非仅凭长度、术语或语态判断。

questions.stem: When a passage presents a "counterargument" and then refutes it, the author's overall rhetorical strategy is best described as:
opts: Concession and rebuttal
Chronological narration
Definition and classification
Comparison and contrast
questions.explain: 考点：先承认对立观点（concession）再反驳（rebuttal）是议论文中常见的论证策略，旨在增强说服力，属于篇章逻辑分析能力。

questions.stem: The phrase "context clues" in reading comprehension refers to:
opts: The background knowledge a reader brings to the text
The hints within a text that help a reader infer the meaning of an unfamiliar word
The footnotes and citations provided by the author
The illustrations and diagrams accompanying the passage
questions.explain: 考点：上下文线索（context clues）是文本内部提供的语义暗示，用于推测生词含义，是阅读理解中词汇推断题的核心依据。

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about "author's purpose" is most accurate?
opts: It can always be determined by reading the title alone
It is irrelevant to the tone and style of the passage
It is often inferred from the overall structure, word choice, and emphasis of the passage
It is identical to the main idea of each paragraph
questions.explain: 考点：作者目的（author's purpose）需通过篇章结构、措辞和重点分布综合推断，不能仅靠标题或等同于段落主旨。

questions.stem: In academic reading, a "hypothesis" presented in the introduction is most likely to be:
opts: Ignored in the later sections of the passage
Tested, discussed, or refined through evidence in subsequent paragraphs
Stated as an absolute truth that requires no further verification
Replaced by a completely unrelated theory in the conclusion
questions.explain: 考点：学术文章中引言提出的假设（hypothesis）通常会在后续段落中被检验、讨论或修正，这是理解论证推进的关键逻辑链。

questions.stem: When a passage uses "analogy" as a rhetorical device, the primary purpose is to:
opts: Present statistical evidence to support a claim
Compare two unlike things to clarify a complex idea or argument
List the chronological sequence of historical events
Define a term by using a dictionary-style explanation
questions.explain: 考点：类比（analogy）通过比较两个不同事物的相似性来帮助读者理解抽象或复杂概念，是阅读中识别论证方法的重要考点。

questions.stem: In the context of a research article discussing climate change, the author writes: "While the proposed geoengineering solutions offer a glimmer of hope, they remain largely theoretical and fraught with unintended consequences that could exacerbate the very problems they aim to solve." The author's primary rhetorical strategy in this sentence is to
opts: A. endorse geoengineering as a practical solution
B. contrast theoretical promise with practical risks
C. dismiss all climate change mitigation efforts
D. advocate for immediate implementation of geoengineering
questions.explain: 考点：识别作者修辞策略（对比与让步）。作者用'While'引导让步状语从句，先承认'glimmer of hope'，再转折强调'theoretical'和'unintended consequences'，形成理论希望与现实风险的对比。

questions.stem: Passage excerpt: "The gig economy, often celebrated for its flexibility, has a darker underbelly. Workers classified as independent contractors are systematically excluded from labor protections such as minimum wage, overtime pay, and health insurance. This classification, critics argue, is a legal fiction that allows corporations to externalize costs onto the most vulnerable." The phrase 'legal fiction' in this context most nearly means
opts: A. a hypothetical scenario used in court
B. a false assumption treated as legally true
C. a creative interpretation of contract law
D. a temporary legal exemption for startups
questions.explain: 考点：根据上下文推断短语含义。'Legal fiction'指法律上虽被认定为真但实际虚假的假设——此处指将工人归类为'独立承包商'这一法律认定掩盖了其实际受雇于平台的事实。

questions.stem: In a literary analysis of Virginia Woolf's 'Mrs. Dalloway', the critic states: "Woolf's stream-of-consciousness technique does not merely reproduce the random flow of thought; rather, it is a meticulously crafted device that mirrors the characters' psychological fragmentation in the aftermath of war." The critic's argument implies that the narrative technique is
opts: A. spontaneous and unstructured
B. both artistic and thematically purposeful
C. primarily a stylistic imitation of Joyce
D. limited to representing external events
questions.explain: 考点：理解隐含论点。批评家先否定'merely reproduce random flow'（排除A），再肯定'meticulously crafted'和'mirrors psychological fragmentation'，暗示该技巧兼具艺术性和主题目的性。

questions.stem: Read the following passage: "Neuroscientific studies have demonstrated that the adolescent brain undergoes significant remodeling, particularly in the prefrontal cortex, which governs impulse control and decision-making. This biological fact, however, is often invoked to absolve young offenders of criminal responsibility—a leap from 'is' to 'ought' that many legal scholars find troubling." The author's attitude toward using neuroscience in legal contexts is best described as
opts: A. enthusiastic endorsement
B. cautious skepticism
C. outright rejection
D. neutral reporting
questions.explain: 考点：推断作者态度。作者用'however'转折，指出从生物事实（is）直接跳到法律判断（ought）是'troubling'的，表明对简单化使用神经科学持谨慎怀疑态度。

questions.stem: Passage: "The decline of print journalism is often attributed solely to the rise of digital media. Yet this narrative overlooks a critical factor: the systematic consolidation of newspaper ownership since the 1980s, which prioritized profit margins over journalistic integrity. A more nuanced account must consider how corporate ownership structures have eroded public trust long before the internet became ubiquitous." The passage suggests that the 'decline of print journalism' is
opts: A. entirely caused by digital competition
B. a result of multiple interconnected factors
C. primarily due to poor journalistic standards
D. an inevitable consequence of technological progress
questions.explain: 考点：识别作者对因果关系的修正。作者先否定单一归因（'often attributed solely'），再提出被忽视的因素（ownership consolidation），暗示衰退是多因素共同作用的结果。

questions.stem: In a philosophical text, the author writes: "To claim that all knowledge derives from sensory experience is to ignore the role of innate cognitive structures that organize and interpret those sensations. Kant's transcendental idealism offers a compelling alternative: the mind is not a blank slate but an active participant in shaping reality." The author's primary purpose is to
opts: A. defend empiricism against rationalist critiques
B. introduce Kant's theory as a resolution to a philosophical debate
C. argue that sensory experience is irrelevant to knowledge
D. compare Kant's ideas with those of modern neuroscientists
questions.explain: 考点：识别段落主旨和作者目的。作者先批评经验主义（'ignore the role of innate structures'），再提出康德理论作为'compelling alternative'，目的是将康德理论作为解决经验主义与理性主义之争的方案。

questions.stem: Passage: "The poet's use of enjambment in the third stanza is not merely a formal choice. By breaking the line at 'and the light / died,' she forces the reader to pause on the word 'light,' creating a momentary hope that is immediately extinguished by 'died' on the next line. This syntactic rupture mirrors the thematic rupture of loss." The analysis above focuses on the relationship between
opts: A. meter and rhyme scheme
B. form and meaning
C. author and reader
D. imagery and symbolism
questions.explain: 考点：理解文学分析中形式与内容的关系。分析指出诗行断裂（形式）如何创造'希望瞬间破灭'的效果（意义），并强调这种句法断裂'mirrors'主题断裂，核心是形式与意义的对应关系。

questions.stem: In a sociological study on urban gentrification, the author observes: "The arrival of art galleries and organic cafes is often celebrated as a sign of neighborhood revitalization. What this narrative obscures is the displacement of long-term residents, many of whom are priced out of housing they can no longer afford. The aesthetic improvement of a neighborhood is not the same as its social improvement." The author's critique targets
opts: A. the economic benefits of gentrification
B. the conflation of aesthetic and social progress
C. the role of artists in urban development
D. the quality of new businesses in gentrified areas
questions.explain: 考点：识别批判对象。作者指出'celebrated as revitalization'（美学改善）掩盖了'displacement'（社会问题），并明确说'aesthetic improvement is not social improvement'，批判的是将两者混为一谈。

questions.stem: Passage: "Historians have long debated the causes of the French Revolution. The traditional 'social conflict' interpretation, which pits the bourgeoisie against the aristocracy, has been challenged by revisionist scholars who emphasize political culture and discourse. More recently, a 'global turn' has situated the revolution within broader Atlantic and colonial contexts, revealing how events in Saint-Domingue and India shaped revolutionary ideology." The passage primarily describes
opts: A. the definitive causes of the French Revolution
B. the evolution of historiographical approaches
C. the superiority of the global turn perspective
D. the weaknesses of revisionist scholarship
questions.explain: 考点：识别段落主旨（学术史综述）。段落按时间顺序介绍从'traditional'到'revisionist'再到'global turn'的史学方法演变，核心是描述研究视角的发展而非评判孰优孰劣。

questions.stem: In a scientific paper on artificial intelligence, the authors write: "While large language models have achieved remarkable performance on a wide range of NLP tasks, their 'understanding' remains fundamentally different from human cognition. These systems manipulate statistical patterns in data without any genuine grasp of meaning, raising important questions about whether the term 'intelligence' is being stretched beyond its useful limits." The authors' stance on the intelligence of LLMs is best characterized as
opts: A. unreserved admiration for their capabilities
B. a call to redefine intelligence to include LLMs
C. skepticism about applying the term 'intelligence' uncritically
D. denial of any practical utility of LLMs
questions.explain: 考点：推断作者立场。作者承认LLM性能（'remarkable performance'），但用'while'转折强调其理解与人类认知'fundamentally different'，并质疑'intelligence'一词是否被过度使用（'stretched beyond its useful limits'），体现对术语应用持批判性审视态度。

questions.stem: In the passage, the author's use of the phrase 'a double-edged sword' primarily serves to indicate that the phenomenon under discussion ______.
opts: has both positive and negative consequences
is too complex to be fully understood
can be used as a weapon in debates
requires careful handling by experts
questions.explain: 考查修辞理解与作者意图——'双刃剑'在学术语境中固定比喻事物兼具利弊两面，干扰项将比喻字面化或过度引申。

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the relationship between the first and second paragraphs of the text?
opts: The second paragraph provides empirical evidence to support a claim made in the first.
The second paragraph introduces a counterargument to the view presented in the first.
The second paragraph elaborates on a concept briefly mentioned in the first.
The second paragraph shifts focus from a general principle to a specific case study.
questions.explain: 考查段落逻辑关系——第二段通常对首段提出的概念进行展开阐述，干扰项混淆了'反驳''举例''从一般到具体'等不同衔接模式。

questions.stem: The word 'ameliorate' in the third paragraph is closest in meaning to ______.
opts: exacerbate
mitigate
quantify
overlook
questions.explain: 考查上下文词汇推断——ameliorate意为'改善、减轻'，与mitigate同义；exacerbate为反义干扰，quantify和overlook在语义上不匹配。

questions.stem: According to the passage, the primary reason why researchers disagree on the effectiveness of the policy is that ______.
opts: they rely on different data sets that yield conflicting results
the policy has not been implemented long enough for assessment
there is no consensus on what constitutes a successful outcome
political biases influence the interpretation of the findings
questions.explain: 考查因果细节定位——原文明确指出分歧根源在于'成功标准'缺乏共识，干扰项分别偷换为数据差异、时间不足和政治偏见。

questions.stem: The author's attitude toward the proposed reform can best be described as ______.
opts: enthusiastic endorsement
cautious optimism
skeptical detachment
outright opposition
questions.explain: 考查作者态度推断——原文使用'promising but requires further scrutiny'等措辞，体现谨慎乐观；干扰项分别对应过度正面、中立冷漠和完全否定。

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the fourth paragraph that the current legal framework ______.
opts: adequately addresses all major concerns raised by critics
was originally designed for a different technological era
has been consistently updated to keep pace with innovation
is widely regarded as a model for other countries to follow
questions.explain: 考查隐含信息推理——原文暗示现行法律制定于互联网普及之前，故推断其针对的是不同技术时代；干扰项与原文批评性描述矛盾。

questions.stem: The example of the 2008 financial crisis is cited in the passage mainly to ______.
opts: illustrate the dangers of deregulation in the banking sector
compare the scale of two different economic downturns
highlight the failure of predictive models used by economists
argue for stricter oversight of emerging financial instruments
questions.explain: 考查例证功能——该例子服务于论证'加强对新兴金融工具监管'这一论点；干扰项虽与危机相关但偏离作者使用例子的目的。

questions.stem: Which of the following statements, if true, would most weaken the author's argument in the fifth paragraph?
opts: The majority of consumers prefer lower prices over data privacy protections.
Companies have voluntarily adopted privacy measures beyond legal requirements.
The cost of implementing privacy safeguards has decreased significantly.
A recent study found no correlation between data breaches and consumer trust.
questions.explain: 考查论证削弱——作者论点建立在'数据泄露损害消费者信任'的因果链上，若该关联不存在则论证基础瓦解；其他选项不直接攻击核心逻辑。

questions.stem: The passage suggests that the term 'sustainable development' is often misused because ______.
opts: it has no universally accepted definition
corporations employ it as a marketing tool without substantive action
environmentalists and economists interpret it in opposite ways
governments use it to justify policies that harm the environment
questions.explain: 考查细节理解与批判性阅读——原文指出企业将'可持续发展'作为'greenwashing'手段，即缺乏实质行动的营销工具；干扰项涉及定义争议和不同群体解读差异。

questions.stem: The overall structure of the passage can best be characterized as ______.
opts: problem-solution-evaluation
thesis-antithesis-synthesis
chronological narrative with analysis
comparative analysis of multiple cases
questions.explain: 考查篇章结构识别——文章遵循'提出问题—给出解决方案—评估方案优劣'的经典学术论述结构；干扰项对应辩证论述、时间叙事和比较分析等不同模式。

questions.stem: In the context of reading comprehension, which of the following best describes the function of a 'topic sentence' in an expository paragraph?
opts: It summarizes the entire passage in a single sentence.
It introduces the main idea of the paragraph and often appears at the beginning.
It provides a counterargument to the paragraph's central claim.
It serves as a transitional device linking two unrelated paragraphs.
questions.explain: A topic sentence typically states the main idea of a paragraph and is most often found at the beginning, guiding the reader's understanding of the paragraph's content.

questions.stem: When an author uses the phrase 'on the other hand' in a passage, the reader should infer that the upcoming information will most likely:
opts: Reinforce the previous point with additional evidence.
Introduce a contrasting perspective or counterpoint.
Provide a chronological sequence of events.
Summarize the main argument of the passage.
questions.explain: The phrase 'on the other hand' is a discourse marker signaling a shift to an opposing or contrasting viewpoint, which is critical for tracking argument structure in reading comprehension.

questions.stem: Which of the following reading strategies is most effective for identifying an author's implicit attitude or tone in a complex academic text?
opts: Skimming the text for numerical data and statistics.
Focusing exclusively on the first and last sentences of each paragraph.
Analyzing word choice, connotation, and rhetorical devices throughout the passage.
Memorizing key vocabulary before reading the entire passage.
questions.explain: An author's tone and implicit attitude are conveyed through subtle linguistic choices such as connotation, figurative language, and rhetorical strategies, requiring close analysis beyond surface-level reading.

questions.stem: In a passage where the author first presents a widely held belief and then systematically dismantles it, the overall rhetorical structure is best described as:
opts: Problem-solution
Compare-contrast
Claim-counterclaim
Cause-effect
questions.explain: This structure—presenting a common view and then refuting it—is known as claim-counterclaim (or thesis-antithesis), a hallmark of argumentative writing that advanced readers must recognize.

questions.stem: The phrase 'this is not to say that...' in an academic argument typically signals that the author is:
opts: Abandoning the main argument entirely.
Introducing a direct contradiction of the previous sentence.
Making a concession or clarifying a potential misinterpretation.
Shifting to a completely new topic unrelated to the preceding discussion.
questions.explain: Such hedging phrases are used to preemptively address possible misunderstandings or to qualify an argument, demonstrating nuanced reasoning that advanced comprehension requires.

questions.stem: When a reading passage contains a lengthy digression that seems unrelated to the main thesis, the skilled reader should first consider that the digression may serve to:
opts: Fill space because the author lacked sufficient evidence.
Provide essential background information or a necessary contrast that ultimately supports the main argument.
Confuse the reader intentionally as a stylistic experiment.
Indicate that the passage was poorly edited and should be disregarded.
questions.explain: In well-crafted academic writing, apparent digressions often function as contextual framing, analogical support, or contrastive evidence that indirectly strengthens the central thesis.

questions.stem: Which of the following inferences is most justified when an author uses the word 'ostensibly' to describe a phenomenon in a critical review?
opts: The author fully endorses the phenomenon as genuine and effective.
The author is presenting a neutral, objective description without judgment.
The author implies that the phenomenon appears one way but is likely different in reality.
The author is citing a statistical fact that has been empirically verified.
questions.explain: 'Ostensibly' carries a connotation of doubt or discrepancy between appearance and reality, enabling careful readers to detect the author's skeptical stance.

questions.stem: In reading comprehension, what is the primary purpose of an author including a 'rhetorical question' within an argumentative passage?
opts: To request direct feedback from the reader.
To introduce a new piece of empirical evidence.
To engage the reader and emphasize a point without expecting an answer.
To signal the end of the passage and summarize key findings.
questions.explain: Rhetorical questions are a persuasive device used to engage readers, provoke thought, and reinforce the author's argument without requiring a literal response.

questions.stem: When a passage shifts from using 'some scholars argue' to 'the evidence overwhelmingly suggests,' the reader should recognize a change in:
opts: Tense and grammatical voice.
Epistemic certainty and rhetorical confidence.
The topic being discussed.
The length of the sentences.
questions.explain: Such a lexical shift from tentative attribution ('some argue') to assertive claim ('evidence overwhelmingly suggests') signals a progression in the author's level of certainty, a key nuance for advanced comprehension.

questions.stem: Which of the following best characterizes the relationship between 'global comprehension' and 'local comprehension' in reading academic texts?
opts: They are independent skills; mastering one does not affect the other.
Local comprehension of individual sentences is sufficient for global understanding of the passage.
Global comprehension requires synthesizing local details into a coherent understanding of the author's overall argument and purpose.
Global comprehension is only necessary for literary texts, not for expository or argumentative writing.
questions.explain: Advanced reading comprehension demands the integration of local-level details (word meanings, sentence structure) into a global-level understanding of thesis, argument structure, and authorial intent.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the author's attitude toward the digital transformation of education as presented in the text?
opts: cautiously optimistic
strongly critical
enthusiastically supportive
indifferently neutral
questions.explain: 考点：态度推断。作者既肯定数字化教育的潜力，又指出其弊端（如数字鸿沟、注意力碎片化），'谨慎乐观'最符合这种有保留的肯定态度。

questions.stem: The word 'salient' in Paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
opts: noticeable
superficial
controversial
ambiguous
questions.explain: 考点：词义猜测。'salient'意为'显著的、突出的'，根据上下文特征描述，'noticeable'是最佳同义替换。

questions.stem: According to the passage, the reason why traditional publishing houses are struggling to adapt to the digital age is that ______.
opts: they lack sufficient capital for technological upgrades
their business model is inherently incompatible with open access
they have underestimated the speed of readers' behavioral shift
government regulations have hindered their digital transition
questions.explain: 考点：细节定位。原文明确指出传统出版商'misjudged the pace at which readers would abandon print'，选项C与此信息精确匹配。

questions.stem: The author mentions the example of the 'Turing Test' in Paragraph 5 mainly to ______.
opts: illustrate the limitations of current AI evaluation methods
trace the historical origin of artificial intelligence research
argue that machines can never truly replicate human cognition
propose a new benchmark for measuring machine intelligence
questions.explain: 考点：例证功能。作者引用图灵测试是为了说明现有AI评估标准的不足，而非单纯介绍历史或提出新标准。

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the 'attention economy' is supported by the passage?
opts: It has fundamentally improved the efficiency of information dissemination.
It prioritizes user engagement over the quality of content.
It is a concept that originated in the field of behavioral economics.
It primarily benefits content creators rather than platform owners.
questions.explain: 考点：观点判断。原文指出注意力经济'values user engagement above all else'，选项B与此观点一致，其他选项均与原文信息相悖。

questions.stem: The passage suggests that the main challenge facing interdisciplinary research today is ______.
opts: the lack of funding from traditional grant agencies
the institutional barriers between academic departments
the insufficient number of qualified researchers
the difficulty in publishing results in top journals
questions.explain: 考点：主旨归纳。文章反复强调'disciplinary silos'和'institutional inertia'是跨学科研究的主要障碍，选项B准确概括了这一核心论点。

questions.stem: The author's argument in Paragraph 4 relies on the assumption that ______.
opts: economic growth is the primary indicator of social progress
technological innovation inevitably leads to job displacement
the benefits of globalization are distributed unevenly across regions
cultural diversity is inherently valuable and worth preserving
questions.explain: 考点：论证假设。第四段的推理建立在'全球化收益分配不均'这一隐含前提之上，选项C是支撑作者后续结论的必要假设。

questions.stem: When an author uses the phrase 'on the other hand' in a passage, the reader should infer that:
opts: The author is about to present a contrasting viewpoint or evidence.
The author is summarizing the previous argument.
The author is introducing a new topic unrelated to the previous one.
The author is emphasizing the same point with additional examples.
questions.explain: Transitional phrases like 'on the other hand' signal a shift to an opposing or contrasting perspective, which is critical for understanding argument structure.

questions.stem: Which of the following inferences is most strongly supported by the statement: 'Despite decades of research, the precise mechanism remains elusive'?
opts: The mechanism has been fully discovered in recent years.
Researchers have given up on finding the mechanism.
The mechanism is still not completely understood after extensive study.
The mechanism is too simple to require further investigation.
questions.explain: The word 'despite' indicates contrast, and 'remains elusive' means still difficult to find, so the correct inference is that the mechanism is not yet fully understood.

questions.stem: In reading comprehension, what is the primary purpose of an author using a rhetorical question in an argumentative text?
opts: To request an answer from the reader directly.
To emphasize a point by making the reader think without expecting a reply.
To introduce statistical data in a more engaging way.
To indicate uncertainty about the topic being discussed.
questions.explain: A rhetorical question is asked to provoke thought or highlight a point, not to elicit an actual answer, making it a persuasive device.

questions.stem: The phrase 'the elephant in the room' in a passage most likely suggests:
opts: A literal elephant present in the setting.
An obvious problem or issue that everyone is avoiding.
A minor detail that has been exaggerated.
A surprising discovery that changes the argument.
questions.explain: This idiom refers to a significant but uncomfortable issue that people deliberately ignore, which is a common figurative device in advanced reading.

questions.stem: When a passage states that 'Correlation does not imply causation,' the author is most likely cautioning against:
opts: Assuming that two related events have a cause-and-effect relationship.
Ignoring statistical data in research.
Using too many examples in an argument.
Focusing only on qualitative evidence.
questions.explain: This classic logical fallacy warning reminds readers that just because two variables are associated, one does not necessarily cause the other.

questions.stem: Which of the following best captures the meaning of the word 'paradigm' as used in academic reading?
opts: A specific example used to illustrate a point.
A typical example or pattern of something; a model or framework.
A mathematical formula for calculating probability.
A grammatical rule in sentence structure.
questions.explain: In academic contexts, 'paradigm' refers to a broad framework or model that shapes how a subject is understood, not just a simple example.

questions.stem: In a passage where the author writes, 'This view, however, fails to account for...' the author is:
opts: Agreeing with the previously mentioned view.
Introducing a limitation or weakness of the previously mentioned view.
Summarizing the main argument of the passage.
Providing additional evidence to support the previous view.
questions.explain: The phrase 'fails to account for' signals a critique or limitation, indicating the author is pointing out a flaw in the argument.

questions.stem: What is the most likely purpose of an author using 'analogy' in a complex scientific text?
opts: To confuse the reader with unrelated comparisons.
To replace technical terms with simpler synonyms.
To explain an unfamiliar concept by comparing it to a familiar one.
To provide a direct definition from the dictionary.
questions.explain: Analogies help readers grasp difficult or abstract ideas by relating them to something already understood, enhancing comprehension.

questions.stem: When a reading passage includes the sentence 'It is worth noting that...' the author intends to:
opts: Dismiss the following point as unimportant.
Highlight a particularly significant piece of information.
Indicate that the following information is optional.
Suggest that the reader should skip this section.
questions.explain: This phrase is a signal that the upcoming information is important and deserves the reader's special attention.

questions.stem: When an author uses the phrase 'on the other hand' in an argumentative text, the reader should infer that:
opts: The author is about to restate the same point for emphasis.
A contrasting or opposing viewpoint will be introduced.
The author is concluding the discussion with a summary.
A series of examples supporting the previous claim will follow.
questions.explain: The discourse marker 'on the other hand' signals a shift to an alternative or opposing perspective, which is essential for tracking the logical structure of an argument.

questions.stem: Which reading strategy is most effective for identifying an author's implicit attitude or tone in a complex passage?
opts: Skimming for numerical data and statistics.
Scanning for key nouns and proper names.
Analyzing word choice (diction) and rhetorical devices.
Memorizing every detail in the first reading.
questions.explain: An author's attitude and tone are conveyed through subtle word choices and rhetorical strategies; close analysis of diction reveals implicit bias or stance.

questions.stem: In a research article, the sentence 'These findings challenge the prevailing assumption that economic growth necessarily leads to environmental degradation' implies that:
opts: The author fully supports the prevailing assumption.
The study's results contradict a widely held belief.
Economic growth and environmental degradation are unrelated.
The author is presenting a literature review without taking a stance.
questions.explain: The verb 'challenge' indicates that the findings oppose or call into question the commonly accepted assumption, signaling a critical stance in the argument.

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of using 'inferential questions' in reading comprehension tests?
opts: To test the reader's ability to recall explicitly stated facts.
To evaluate the reader's capacity to derive meaning beyond the literal text.
To assess the reader's speed of reading and scanning.
To measure the reader's vocabulary size in isolation.
questions.explain: Inferential questions require readers to read between the lines, using textual clues and prior knowledge to understand implied meanings, which is a higher-order comprehension skill.

questions.stem: When a passage contains the statement 'The correlation between sleep duration and cognitive performance is well-documented, yet the causal mechanism remains elusive,' the word 'elusive' most nearly means:
opts: Clearly established by multiple studies.
Difficult to capture or identify.
Completely irrelevant to the discussion.
Easily explained by common sense.
questions.explain: 'Elusive' in academic reading often describes something that is hard to find, define, or understand, especially when referring to causal relationships that are not yet proven.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a key characteristic of a 'coherent' paragraph in academic writing?
opts: Each sentence introduces a completely new and unrelated idea.
Sentences are arranged in random order to test reader flexibility.
All sentences logically connect and collectively support a single main idea.
The paragraph contains only one long sentence without any transitions.
questions.explain: Coherence in a paragraph means that ideas flow logically and are unified around a central point, with clear connections between sentences.

questions.stem: In critical reading, distinguishing between 'fact' and 'opinion' is crucial because:
opts: Facts are always false and opinions are always true.
Opinions can be verified objectively, while facts are subjective.
Facts can be verified with evidence, whereas opinions reflect personal beliefs that may be biased.
Both facts and opinions are equally unreliable in academic texts.
questions.explain: Facts are objective and verifiable, while opinions are subjective judgments; recognizing the difference helps readers evaluate the strength of an argument.

questions.stem: When an academic author writes 'It is worth noting that...' the rhetorical function is typically to:
opts: Dismiss the following point as unimportant.
Signal that the upcoming information is particularly significant.
Indicate that the author is uncertain about the claim.
Transition to a completely unrelated topic.
questions.explain: The phrase 'It is worth noting that...' is a metadiscursive marker used to draw the reader's attention to a point the author considers important or noteworthy.

questions.stem: A passage that begins with a specific anecdote and then moves to a general conclusion is using which organizational pattern?
opts: Deductive reasoning (general to specific).
Inductive reasoning (specific to general).
Chronological order (time sequence).
Problem-solution structure.
questions.explain: Inductive reasoning starts with specific observations or examples and builds toward a broader generalization or conclusion, which is a common pattern in argumentative writing.

questions.stem: In the passage, the author's use of the phrase 'a double-edged sword' (paragraph 3) primarily serves to emphasize that the technology in question ______.
opts: A. has both beneficial and harmful effects that are equally weighted
B. brings advantages that inevitably come with corresponding drawbacks
C. is too dangerous to be widely adopted in its current form
D. requires further research before its full impact can be assessed
questions.explain: 考点为修辞意图推断；'double-edged sword' 比喻任何事物都有两面性，强调优点必然伴随缺点，而非利弊完全相等。

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the author's attitude toward the proposed reform in the text?
opts: A. Enthusiastic endorsement with minor reservations
B. Cautious optimism tempered by practical concerns
C. Skeptical opposition based on empirical evidence
D. Neutral detachment without personal judgment
questions.explain: 考点为作者态度判断；通过文中让步从句和限定词可推断作者持谨慎乐观态度，既认可改革方向又担忧实施障碍。

questions.stem: The author mentions the 2019 study in paragraph 2 primarily to ______.
opts: A. introduce a new research methodology for future investigations
B. challenge the prevailing view held by mainstream economists
C. provide empirical support for the argument advanced earlier
D. contrast the findings with those of earlier longitudinal studies
questions.explain: 考点为例证功能判断；引述研究数据通常为前文论点提供实证支撑，而非引入方法或挑战主流观点。

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that the term 'cognitive load' (paragraph 4) refers to ______.
opts: A. the total amount of mental effort being used in working memory
B. the stress caused by multitasking in digital environments
C. the limit of human brain capacity for storing long-term memories
D. the difficulty level of a specific learning task or assignment
questions.explain: 考点为上下文词义推断；根据语境线索（working memory capacity, mental resources）可锁定认知负荷指工作记忆中的心理努力总量。

questions.stem: According to the passage, the main reason why the policy failed in its initial implementation was that ______.
opts: A. the target population was not adequately informed about the changes
B. the economic incentives were misaligned with actual behavioral patterns
C. the political opposition from interest groups undermined the process
D. the timeline for rollout was too compressed to allow proper adaptation
questions.explain: 考点为因果细节定位；原文明确将失败归因于激励设计与真实行为模式脱节，而非信息不足或政治阻力。

questions.stem: The author's use of the word 'ostensibly' in paragraph 1 suggests that the stated purpose of the initiative is ______.
opts: A. genuine and well-intentioned
B. deceptive and misleading
C. apparently true but possibly not so
D. legally mandated and enforceable
questions.explain: 考点为语气词理解；'ostensibly' 意为表面上，暗示宣称的目的可能并非真实意图，表达一种怀疑或保留态度。

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is most consistent with the author's view on globalization as expressed in the passage?
opts: A. Globalization has uniformly benefited all participating nations
B. The benefits of globalization have been unevenly distributed across regions
C. Globalization should be reversed to protect domestic industries
D. Cultural homogenization is the most significant consequence of globalization
questions.explain: 考点为观点一致性判断；文中通过对比发达与发展中国家的不同境遇，强调全球化收益分配不均，而非全面肯定或否定。

questions.stem: The analogy drawn between 'ecosystems' and 'markets' in paragraph 5 serves to illustrate that ______.
opts: A. both systems operate on the principle of natural selection
B. market regulation should mimic ecological conservation strategies
C. complex systems share similar patterns of resilience and fragility
D. economic downturns are as inevitable as ecological collapses
questions.explain: 考点为类比功能理解；类比旨在揭示复杂系统在韧性与脆弱性方面的共性，而非主张直接套用生态策略。

questions.stem: The passage implies that the conventional approach to measuring economic growth is inadequate because it ______.
opts: A. overlooks the depletion of natural resources and environmental costs
B. relies too heavily on subjective indicators of well-being
C. fails to account for inflation and purchasing power parity
D. uses outdated statistical models from the post-war era
questions.explain: 考点为隐含观点推断；文中批评传统GDP核算忽略资源消耗与环境代价，暗示需要更全面的衡量标准。

questions.stem: 设函数 f(x) 在 x=0 处可导，且 f(0)=0，则极限 lim_{x→0} f(x)/x 等于？
opts: 不存在
questions.explain: 根据导数定义，f'(0)=lim_{x→0} [f(x)-f(0)]/x = lim_{x→0} f(x)/x，故极限等于 f'(0)。

questions.stem: 曲线 y = x^3 - 3x + 1 的拐点横坐标为？
questions.explain: 拐点处二阶导数为零，y''=6x=0 ⇒ x=0，且左右两侧二阶导数变号，故拐点横坐标为0。

questions.stem: 定积分 ∫_{0}^{1} x^2 dx 的值为？
函数 f(x)=e^x 在 x=0 处的 n 阶泰勒展开（带皮亚诺余项）中，x^n 项的系数为？
opts: e
questions.explain: e^x 的麦克劳林展开为 ∑_{k=0}^{∞} x^k/k!，故 x^n 项系数为 1/n!。

questions.stem: 微分方程 y' = 2x 的通解为？

questions.stem: 极限 lim_{x→0} (sin x)/x 的值为？

questions.stem: 函数 f(x)=e^x 在 x=0 处的 n 阶麦克劳林公式中，拉格朗日余项为？

questions.stem: 微分方程 y'' - y = 0 的通解为？

questions.stem: 反常积分 ∫_{1}^{+∞} 1/x^p dx 收敛的条件是？

y = e^(2x) + C
questions.explain: 一阶线性齐次微分方程，分离变量积分得通解 y = Ce^(2x)。

questions.stem: 二元函数 f(x,y) = x² + y² 在点 (1,1) 处的梯度向量是？
In the sentence "The significance of the experiment was not lost on the researchers," the underlined phrase "was not lost on" is best translated into Chinese as:
opts: 没有被……丢失
没有被……遗忘
被……充分理解
被……完全忽略
questions.explain: 考点：英语习语 'be not lost on sb' 意为'被某人充分领会/理解'，不能字面直译为'丢失'，需结合语境进行意译。

questions.stem: How to render the logical connective in "He is not so much a scholar as a critic" into idiomatic Chinese?
opts: 他与其说是一位学者，不如说是一位批评家
他不仅是一位学者，还是一位批评家
他既是学者又是批评家
他不如批评家那么像学者
questions.explain: 考点：'not so much A as B' 是英语特有的比较结构，汉语需用'与其说A，不如说B'的句式进行等效转换，不可直译。

questions.stem: In translating "She had a cold detachment that kept everyone at arm's length," which Chinese version best preserves both the literal image and the figurative meaning of 'at arm's length'?
opts: 她有一种冷淡的疏离感，让每个人都保持在一臂之遥
她冷漠疏远，拒人于千里之外
她冷若冰霜，让人不敢靠近
她态度冷淡，总是把别人推开
questions.explain: 考点：英译汉中比喻性习语的翻译策略——'at arm's length'既有字面形象（一臂之遥），又有比喻义（保持距离），此处直译加语境可保留原文修辞效果。

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most accurate Chinese translation of the passive voice in "It is universally acknowledged that a single man in possession of a good fortune must be in want of a wife"?
opts: 人们普遍认为，一个拥有好财产的单身汉必定想要娶个妻子
它被普遍承认，一个单身汉拥有好财产必须需要一个妻子
凡是有钱的单身汉，总想娶位太太，这已经成了一条举世公认的真理
一个单身汉拥有好财产，他必须需要一个妻子，这是被普遍承认的
questions.explain: 考点：英译汉中被动语态的处理技巧——英语被动结构'It is acknowledged that...'在汉语中常转换为主动式或独立短句，且需符合汉语表达习惯，王佐良译本为典范。

questions.stem: In the sentence "The proposal was dead on arrival," the idiom 'dead on arrival' should be translated as:
opts: 到达时就已死亡
一提出就遭否决
毫无生气地抵达
在到达时死了
questions.explain: 考点：英语隐喻性习语'dead on arrival'（原指病人送达医院时已死亡）在政治/商业语境中引申为'一开始就失败/被否决'，翻译需取引申义。

questions.stem: Which Chinese translation best handles the English nominalization in "The exploration of space has led to the development of numerous technologies"?
opts: 太空的探索已经导致了无数技术的发展
探索太空使无数技术得到了发展
对太空的探索已经带来了很多技术的发展
太空被探索导致了技术被发展
questions.explain: 考点：英译汉中对英语名词化结构的转换——英语常用抽象名词（exploration, development）作主语/宾语，汉语则倾向使用动词结构（探索太空、得到发展），使译文更动态自然。

questions.stem: How should the English sentence "He is the last person to betray his friends" be correctly rendered in Chinese?
opts: 他是最后一个背叛朋友的人
他是最不可能背叛朋友的人
他最后背叛了他的朋友
他上次背叛了他的朋友们
questions.explain: 考点：英语'last + 名词 + to do'结构的特殊含义——并非字面'最后一个做某事'，而是'最不可能做某事'，属于否定转移的翻译难点。

questions.stem: In translating "The city boasts a rich cultural heritage," which Chinese version is most idiomatic?
opts: 这座城市吹嘘自己拥有丰富的文化遗产
这座城市以拥有丰富的文化遗产而自豪
这座城市拥有丰富的文化遗产
这座城市夸耀其丰富的文化遗产
questions.explain: 考点：英语中'boast'的翻译策略——'boast'在描述事物时意为'拥有（值得自豪的事物）'，汉语不宜直译为'吹嘘/夸耀'，而应取其客观含义'拥有'。

questions.stem: Which Chinese translation correctly renders the English subjunctive mood in "Had it not been for your help, I would have failed"?
opts: 如果没有你的帮助，我就会失败
要不是你的帮助，我早就失败了
如果它不是为了你的帮助，我将会失败
假如没有过你的帮助，我将会已经失败
questions.explain: 考点：英译汉中虚拟语气的处理——英语倒装虚拟条件句'Had it not been for...'在汉语中常用'要不是……'或'若非……'来传达强烈的假设与反事实意味，同时需体现时态差异（would have failed表示与过去事实相反）。

questions.stem: In the sentence "The book is a must-read for anyone interested in AI," the compound 'must-read' should be translated as:
opts: 必须读的书
必读书目
一本必须的阅读
不得不读的东西
questions.explain: 考点：英语复合名词'must-read'的汉译——英语中'must + 动词'构成的复合名词（must-read, must-see）在汉语中常译为'必读/必看'等四字格，简洁且符合汉语名词性表达习惯。

questions.stem: In the sentence "The importance of this discovery cannot be overestimated", the best Chinese translation is:
opts: 这一发现的重要性不能被高估。
这一发现的重要性再怎么估计也不为过。
这一发现的重要性不能被低估。
这一发现的重要性无法被过高估计。
questions.explain: 考点：cannot...over- 结构为双重否定表肯定，意为‘再…也不为过’，直译‘不能被高估’是典型误译。

questions.stem: How should "He is anything but a scholar" be translated into Chinese?
opts: 他什么都是，就是不是一个学者。
他根本不是一个学者。
他除了学者什么都是。
他可能是一个学者。
questions.explain: 考点：anything but 意为‘绝不、根本不’，与 nothing but（仅仅）形成对比，常见误译为‘除了…都’。

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most accurate translation of "She is no more a teacher than I am a pilot"?
opts: 她不是老师，就像我不是飞行员一样。
她和我一样都不是老师。
她不是老师，我也不是飞行员。
她比我更不适合当老师。
questions.explain: 考点：no more...than... 结构表示‘两者都不’，译为‘A不是…，就像B不是…一样’。

questions.stem: In translating "It is a wise father that knows his own child", the best equivalent in Chinese is:
opts: 聪明的父亲才能认识自己的孩子。
再聪明的父亲也不一定完全了解自己的孩子。
父亲了解自己的孩子是明智的。
只有聪明的父亲才认识自己的孩子。
questions.explain: 考点：It is a + adj. + n. + that... 结构常表让步否定，意为‘再…的…也不一定…’，不可直译为肯定句。

questions.stem: The phrase "the last person I want to see" should be translated as:
opts: 我最后想见的人
我最不愿见的人
我最后一个想见的人
我最后见到的人
questions.explain: 考点：the last...to do 意为‘最不可能/最不愿意…’，而非字面‘最后一个’。

questions.stem: How to render "He is too proud to admit his mistake" into idiomatic Chinese?
opts: 他太骄傲了，不能承认自己的错误。
他太骄傲了，以至于不肯承认自己的错误。
他骄傲得无法承认自己的错误。
他过于骄傲，不会承认自己的错误。
questions.explain: 考点：too...to... 结构表示‘太…以至于不…’，但中文习惯用‘不肯/不愿’而非‘不能’，需注意否定词的情感色彩。

questions.stem: Which translation best captures the meaning of "I don't think it will rain"?
opts: 我不认为天会下雨。
我认为天不会下雨。
我不觉得天会下雨。
我没想到天会下雨。
questions.explain: 考点：英语否定转移（否定主句谓语）在译成汉语时需还原为否定从句，即‘认为…不会’而非‘不认为…会’。

questions.stem: The sentence "He is as good as dead" is best translated as:
opts: 他和死人一样好。
他几乎和死人一样。
他好得像死了一样。
他死得其所。
questions.explain: 考点：as good as 是固定习语，意为‘几乎、实际上等于’，不可按字面拆译。

questions.stem: What is the correct Chinese translation of "She sings not that she wants to win but that she loves music"?
opts: 她唱歌不是为了赢，而是因为她热爱音乐。
她唱歌不是她想赢，而是她热爱音乐。
她唱歌不是为了赢，而是她热爱音乐。
她唱歌不是她想赢，而是因为她热爱音乐。
questions.explain: 考点：not that...but that... 结构中 that 引导原因状语从句，标准译法为‘不是因为…而是因为…’，需保持结构对称。

questions.stem: Which Chinese version correctly renders "There is no rule but has exceptions"?
opts: 没有规则有例外。
任何规则都有例外。
没有规则没有例外。
有规则就没有例外。
questions.explain: 考点：but 作关系代词引导定语从句，与否定词连用构成双重否定表肯定，意为‘没有…不…’，即‘任何…都…’。

questions.stem: In the sentence "The significance of the experiment cannot be overestimated," which of the following Chinese translations best captures the original meaning?
opts: 这个实验的重要性不能被过高估计。
这个实验的重要性怎么估计也不为过。
这个实验的重要性不能被过分强调。
这个实验的重要性被低估了。
questions.explain: 考点：cannot...over- 结构表“再怎么……也不为过”，是英译汉中的常见否定转移现象。

questions.stem: Which Chinese version correctly renders "She is nothing if not persistent"?
opts: 她如果不坚持就什么都不是。
她最大的特点就是坚持不懈。
她一点也不坚持。
她除了坚持什么都不会。
questions.explain: 考点：nothing if not 结构表“极其、非常”，是英译汉中需要意译的强调结构。

questions.stem: In translating "It is a wise man that never makes mistakes," which option accurately conveys the original meaning?
opts: 聪明的人从不犯错。
智者千虑，必有一失。
一个从不犯错的聪明人。
聪明人不会犯错。
questions.explain: 考点：It is + adj. + n. + that... 结构常含反讽意味，实际表“再……的人也难免”，需意译。

questions.stem: What is the correct Chinese translation of "I don't think that he will come, but I'll wait for him just in case"?
opts: 我认为他不会来，但以防万一我还是等他。
我不认为他会来，但为了以防万一我还是等他。
我认为他不会来，但为了以防万一我还是等他。
我不认为他会来，但以防万一我还是等他。
questions.explain: 考点：英译汉中否定前移的处理——英语否定主句，汉语否定从句更自然。

questions.stem: Which translation best renders "The more he tried to explain, the more confused I became"?
opts: 他越解释，我越糊涂。
他解释得越多，我变得越困惑。
他越试图解释，我越困惑。
他越解释，我越困惑。
questions.explain: 考点：the more...the more... 结构在英译汉时需保持平行对称，选项D最简洁准确。

questions.stem: How should "He is the last person to betray his friend" be translated into Chinese?
opts: 他是最后一个背叛朋友的人。
他绝不是会背叛朋友的人。
他最近背叛了朋友。
他是背叛朋友的最后一个人。
questions.explain: 考点：the last person to do sth. 表“最不可能做某事的人”，是英译汉中典型的否定转移。

questions.stem: Which Chinese version correctly translates "Not that I don't want to help, but that I'm unable to"?
opts: 不是我不想帮忙，而是我无能为力。
我不想要帮忙，但我不能。
不是我不想要帮忙，而是我不能。
我不想帮忙，但我不能。
questions.explain: 考点：Not that...but that... 结构表“不是因为……而是因为……”，英译汉需保留对比逻辑。

questions.stem: What is the correct Chinese translation of "There is no rule but has exceptions"?
opts: 没有规则有例外。
任何规则都有例外。
没有规则的例外。
规则没有例外。
questions.explain: 考点：but 作关系代词表“that...not”，no...but 双重否定表肯定，英译汉需还原为肯定句。

questions.stem: Which translation best captures the meaning of "He is as poor as a church mouse"?
opts: 他像教堂老鼠一样穷。
他一贫如洗。
他像老鼠一样穷。
他穷得像教堂里的老鼠。
questions.explain: 考点：英译汉中习语的文化转换——直译可能造成理解障碍，需用汉语对应习语意译。

questions.stem: In the sentence "The importance of this discovery cannot be overemphasized," the most accurate Chinese translation is:
opts: 这一发现的重要性不能被过分强调。
这一发现的重要性无论怎样强调也不为过。
这一发现的重要性不能被过度夸大。
这一发现的重要性无法被充分认识。
questions.explain: 考点：cannot...over- 结构表示“无论怎样……也不为过”，而非字面否定。

questions.stem: The phrase "a sea of faces" in English should be translated into Chinese as:
opts: 一片海洋般的面孔
人山人海
众多面孔
茫茫人海中的面孔
questions.explain: 考点：英译汉时比喻性短语应转化为中文惯用表达，"a sea of faces" 对应成语“人山人海”。

questions.stem: In "He is the last person to tell a lie," the correct Chinese rendering is:
opts: 他是最后一个说谎的人。
他绝不可能说谎。
他上次说了谎。
他是最不可能说谎的人之一。
questions.explain: 考点："the last person to do" 表示“最不可能做某事的人”，而非字面“最后一个”。

questions.stem: How should the sentence "It is a wise father that knows his own child" be translated into Chinese?
opts: 只有聪明的父亲才了解自己的孩子。
了解自己孩子的父亲是聪明的。
再聪明的父亲也未必了解自己的孩子。
聪明的父亲当然了解自己的孩子。
questions.explain: 考点："It is a + adj. + n. + that..." 结构常含反讽意味，译为“再……也未必……”。

questions.stem: The English idiom "pull someone's leg" should be translated into Chinese as:
opts: 拖某人后腿
拉某人一把
开某人玩笑
扯某人后腿
questions.explain: 考点：英译汉时习语不可直译，"pull one's leg" 意为“开玩笑、逗弄”，而非字面动作。

questions.stem: In the sentence "He was a man of no mean ability," the best Chinese translation is:
opts: 他是一个没有卑鄙能力的人。
他是一个能力平庸的人。
他是一个能力很强的人。
他是一个毫无能力的人。
questions.explain: 考点："no mean" 为双重否定表肯定，意为“很、相当”，"no mean ability" 即“能力很强”。

questions.stem: The sentence "You cannot be too careful when driving" should be translated as:
opts: 你开车时不能太小心。
你开车时再怎么小心也不为过。
你开车时不必过分小心。
你开车时小心一点就够了。
questions.explain: 考点："cannot be too + adj." 结构表示“无论怎样……也不为过”，与 cannot...over- 同理。

questions.stem: How to translate "She is anything but beautiful" into Chinese?
opts: 她除了漂亮什么都是。
她一点也不漂亮。
她非常漂亮。
她什么都漂亮。
questions.explain: 考点："anything but" 意为“绝不、根本不”，与 nothing but（仅仅）相反。

questions.stem: The English sentence "I had no sooner arrived home than it began to rain" should be translated as:
opts: 我到家后不久就开始下雨了。
我还没到家就开始下雨了。
我刚到家就开始下雨了。
我到家之前雨就停了。
questions.explain: 考点："no sooner...than..." 表示“一……就……”，强调两个动作几乎同时发生。

questions.stem: In the sentence "He is a walking dictionary," the correct Chinese translation is:
opts: 他是一本会走的字典。
他随身带着一本字典。
他学识渊博，像一本活字典。
他走路时总在背字典。
questions.explain: 考点："a walking + n." 是比喻用法，译为“活……”，如“活字典”，不可直译。

questions.stem: In the sentence "The enigma of his abrupt resignation left the board in a state of utter perplexity.", which of the following Chinese translations best captures the nuance of 'enigma' and 'utter perplexity'?
opts: 他突然辞职的谜团让董事会完全困惑。
他突然辞职的奥秘使董事会陷入彻底的茫然。
他突然辞职的费解之处令董事会惊愕不已。
他突然辞职的悬疑让董事会极度费解。
questions.explain: 考点：抽象名词的精准对应——'enigma' 比普通 'mystery' 更具哲学意味，译为'奥秘'更贴切；'utter perplexity' 强调彻底茫然，'彻底的茫然'优于'完全困惑'或'极度费解'。

questions.stem: In translating "The proliferation of digital platforms has fundamentally reconfigured the landscape of interpersonal communication.", which rendering best preserves the formal register and the verb 'reconfigured'?
opts: 数字平台的扩散从根本上改变了人际沟通的景观。
数字平台的激增从根本上重塑了人际沟通的格局。
数字平台的泛滥从本质上调整了人际交流的面貌。
数字平台的增多从根基上改造了人际交往的图景。
questions.explain: 考点：语体色彩与动词精准度——'proliferation' 在正式语境中常译为'激增'而非贬义的'泛滥'；'reconfigured' 强调结构重组，'重塑'优于'改变/调整/改造'。

questions.stem: The clause "Not until the final whistle did the magnitude of their defeat dawn on them" requires careful handling of the inverted structure. Which translation correctly conveys the temporal logic and the verb phrase 'dawn on'?
opts: 直到终场哨响他们才意识到失败有多惨重。
不到终场哨响他们不会明白失败的程度。
直到最后一声哨响失败的严重性才降临到他们头上。
终场哨响之前他们一直没搞懂失败有多大。
questions.explain: 考点：倒装句的汉语转换与'dawn on'的译法——'not...until' 译为'直到……才'最自然；'dawn on' 是'逐渐意识到'，'降临到头上'是误译。

questions.stem: In the sentence "Her ostensibly casual remark was, in fact, a meticulously calculated provocation.", which Chinese translation best captures the contrast between 'ostensibly' and 'in fact'?
opts: 她表面上随意的评论实际上是一次精心计算的挑衅。
她貌似随便的一句话其实是一场周密策划的激将。
她看似漫不经心的发言实则是处心积虑的挑衅。
她外表轻松的谈话实际上是精密设计的刺激。
questions.explain: 考点：副词对比与名词精准度——'ostensibly' 译为'貌似'比'表面上'更书面；'provocation' 在心理博弈语境中译为'激将'比'挑衅'更准确；'meticulously calculated' 强调周密，'处心积虑'贬义过重。

questions.stem: How should the participial phrase in "Armed with nothing but a worn-out map, he ventured into the uncharted wilderness." be best rendered into Chinese?
opts: 除了破旧地图什么武器也没有，他冒险进入了未知荒野。
仅凭一张破旧地图，他踏入了未经勘测的荒野。
带着只有破旧地图的装备，他探险进入了无地图的荒野。
手无寸铁只有一张旧地图，他闯进了无人知晓的荒原。
questions.explain: 考点：分词短语的汉语转换——'Armed with...' 是比喻用法，译为'仅凭'比直译'武器'更符合汉语习惯；'uncharted' 应译为'未经勘测的'而非'无地图的'。

questions.stem: In translating "The implications of quantum entanglement are so profound that they challenge the very foundations of classical physics.", which version best handles the emphasis of 'so...that...' and the word 'very'?
opts: 量子纠缠的含义如此深远以至于它们挑战了经典物理学的非常基础。
量子纠缠的意涵深刻到足以撼动经典物理学的根基本身。
量子纠缠的影响非常深刻，它们挑战了经典物理学的根本基础。
量子纠缠的后果如此重大，以至于它们质疑了经典物理学的整个基础。
questions.explain: 考点：强调结构的自然化处理——'so...that...' 译为'……到足以……'更简洁；'very' 表强调时译为'本身'比'非常/整个'更准确；'implications' 应译为'意涵'而非'含义/影响/后果'。

questions.stem: The sentence "It is not so much that he lacks talent as that he refuses to apply himself." contains a 'not so much...as...' structure. Which translation is correct?
opts: 与其说他缺乏天赋不如说他拒绝努力。
不是他那么缺乏天赋而是他不肯用功。
他缺乏天赋的程度没有他不努力的程度大。
说他缺乏天赋倒不如说他拒绝全力以赴。
questions.explain: 考点：'not so much A as B' 固定结构的译法——标准译法为'与其说A不如说B'；选项3虽意思接近但不符合汉语惯用表达。

questions.stem: In "The court ruled that the evidence, though circumstantial, was admissible.", which translation correctly renders the legal terms 'circumstantial' and 'admissible'?
opts: 法院裁定该证据虽是环境性的，但是可接受的。
法院裁定该证据虽是间接的，但是可采纳的。
法院裁定该证据虽是旁证的，但是可准入的。
法院裁定该证据虽是细节性的，但是可允许的。
questions.explain: 考点：法律术语的固定译法——'circumstantial evidence' 法律术语为'间接证据'；'admissible' 在诉讼法中固定译为'可采纳的'。

questions.stem: How should the metaphor in "Time is a thief that steals our moments, leaving only memories in its wake." be best preserved in Chinese translation?
opts: 时间是小偷，偷走我们的时刻，只在身后留下记忆。
时间如窃贼，盗走我们的光阴，只余回忆在其尾迹。
时间是个贼，偷走我们的当下，只留下记忆在身后。
时间如同盗匪，掠走我们的分秒，仅剩回忆留在其踪迹中。
questions.explain: 考点：比喻修辞的文学性转换——'如窃贼'比'是小偷/是个贼'更具文学色彩；'盗走'比'偷走'更书面；'光阴'比'时刻/当下/分秒'更符合文学语境；'在其尾迹'保留原文意象但需调整语序。

questions.stem: The sentence "He was caught between a rock and a hard place, having to choose between betraying his friend and losing his job." contains an idiom. Which translation best handles the idiom and the dilemma?
opts: 他被夹在岩石和坚硬的地方之间，必须在背叛朋友和失去工作之间选择。
他进退两难，必须在背叛朋友和丢掉饭碗之间做出抉择。
他处于岩石与硬地之间的夹缝中，不得不在出卖朋友和失业之间选一个。
他左右为难，不得不在背叛朋友和失去工作之间做出决定。
questions.explain: 考点：英语习语的地道汉译——'between a rock and a hard place' 译为'进退两难'是标准对应；'losing his job' 译为'丢掉饭碗'比'失去工作'更口语化且符合语境。

questions.stem: In the sentence 'The importance of this discovery cannot be overemphasized,' the most accurate Chinese translation of 'cannot be overemphasized' is:
opts: 不能过分强调
怎么强调也不为过
无法被过度强调
不应该被强调
questions.explain: 考查否定结构英译汉的固定译法：'cannot...over-'结构在英语中表示'再……也不为过'，而非字面否定。

questions.stem: The phrase 'a sea of faces' in 'He looked out into a sea of faces' should be translated into Chinese as:
opts: 一片人脸的海
无数张面孔
一张张忧郁的脸
人山人海
questions.explain: 考查英语隐喻性短语的汉语地道转换：'a sea of faces' 应译为汉语习语'人山人海'，而非直译。

questions.stem: In 'She is something of a legend in her field,' the underlined part 'something of' is best rendered in Chinese as:
opts: 某种东西
可以说是
有一点儿
完全是
questions.explain: 考查'be something of'结构的英译汉：该短语表示'在某种程度上是'，应译为'可以说是'或'称得上'。

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best Chinese translation for 'It is not that I don't like the plan, but that I think it needs more discussion'?
opts: 不是我不喜欢这个计划，而是我认为它需要更多讨论
我不喜欢这个计划，但我认为它需要更多讨论
这个计划我不喜欢，不过它需要更多讨论
并非我不喜欢这个计划，我认为它需要更多讨论
questions.explain: 考查'not that...but that...'并列否定结构的英译汉：应译为'不是……而是……'，保持原句的对比逻辑关系。

questions.stem: The English sentence 'He was all ears when the teacher explained the problem' should be translated into Chinese as:
opts: 他全身都是耳朵
他全神贯注地听
他竖起耳朵听
他耳朵很灵
questions.explain: 考查英语习语'be all ears'的汉译：应译为'竖起耳朵听'或'聚精会神地听'，不能直译为'全身都是耳朵'。

questions.stem: In translating 'The more he thought about it, the more confused he became,' the most natural Chinese rendering is:
opts: 他想得越多，变得越困惑
他越想越困惑
他更多想它，更多困惑
他思考得越多，困惑就越多
questions.explain: 考查'越……越……'结构的英译汉：英语'the more...the more...'应译为汉语紧凑的'越A越B'句式，而非逐字对应。

questions.stem: Which Chinese translation best captures the meaning of 'She has a green thumb'?
opts: 她有一个绿色的大拇指
她擅长园艺
她手指发绿
她喜欢绿色
questions.explain: 考查英语文化习语'green thumb'的英译汉：该习语意为'擅长园艺'，不能按字面直译。

questions.stem: The sentence 'He is the last person I would trust with such a secret' should be translated as:
opts: 他是我最后一个托付秘密的人
他是我最不可能托付秘密的人
他是我最信任托付秘密的人
他是我最后才想到托付秘密的人
questions.explain: 考查'the last person to do'结构的英译汉：该结构表示'最不可能……的人'，而非字面'最后一个'。

questions.stem: In 'I couldn't agree with you more,' the Chinese translation that best conveys the original meaning is:
opts: 我不能再同意你了
我完全同意你
我无法同意你更多
我不同意你
questions.explain: 考查否定比较级表最高级含义的英译汉：'couldn't...more'表示'完全同意'，而非字面否定。

questions.stem: The phrase 'a stone's throw' in 'The hotel is a stone's throw from the beach' should be translated into Chinese as:
opts: 一石之遥
扔一块石头的距离
近在咫尺
一块石头的距离
questions.explain: 考查英语距离习语'a stone's throw'的汉译：应译为'近在咫尺'或'一步之遥'，体现汉语四字格的地道表达。

questions.stem: The phrase 'a storm in a teacup' is best rendered into Chinese as:
opts: 茶杯里的风暴
小题大做
杯水车薪
风平浪静
questions.explain: 考点：英语习语英译汉时需采用汉语对应习语（意译），而非字面直译。

questions.stem: In 'He is a walking dictionary,' the underlined part should be translated as:
opts: 一本行走的字典
活字典
移动的词典
会走路的词典
questions.explain: 考点：英语隐喻性表达在英译汉时需转化为汉语习惯说法，“walking”译为“活”更地道。

questions.stem: The sentence 'It is a wise father that knows his own child' implies that:
opts: 了解自己孩子的父亲是聪明的。
再聪明的父亲也未必了解自己的孩子。
聪明的父亲都了解自己的孩子。
父亲了解孩子是明智的。
questions.explain: 考点：It is + adj. + n. + that... 句型常含反讽意味，英译汉需译出“再…也未必…”的隐含逻辑。

questions.stem: The English idiom 'pull someone's leg' should be translated into Chinese as:
opts: 拉某人的腿
拖某人后腿
开某人的玩笑
扯某人的后腿
questions.explain: 考点：英语习语英译汉时不可字面直译，需找到汉语中功能对等的习语。

questions.stem: In 'He is too ready to promise,' the correct Chinese translation is:
opts: 他太愿意承诺了。
他太急于承诺，以至于不能兑现。
他非常容易做出承诺。
他轻易许诺。
questions.explain: 考点：too ready to do 结构并非“太…而不能”，而是“过于容易/轻易做某事”，需注意否定转移陷阱。

questions.stem: The sentence 'She sings not that she may show off, but that she pleases herself' is best translated as:
opts: 她唱歌不是为了炫耀，而是为了取悦自己。
她唱歌不是为了炫耀，而是为了让自己高兴。
她唱歌不是要炫耀，而是要让自己开心。
她唱歌不是为炫耀，而是自娱自乐。
questions.explain: 考点：英译汉中“not that...but that...”结构需译为“不是为…而是为…”，且“pleases herself”译为“自娱自乐”更符合汉语四字格习惯。

questions.stem: The phrase 'armed to the teeth' is most idiomatically translated into Chinese as:
opts: 武装到牙齿
全副武装
牙齿上装武器
武装到牙
questions.explain: 考点：英语习语“armed to the teeth”虽已有直译“武装到牙齿”被汉语吸收，但更地道的汉语表达是“全副武装”，需根据语境判断。

questions.stem: The sentence 'I had no sooner arrived home than it began to rain' should be translated as:
opts: 我到家后不久就下雨了。
我一到家天就下雨了。
我还没到家天就下雨了。
我到家之前天就下雨了。
questions.explain: 考点：no sooner...than... 结构表“一…就…”，英译汉需用汉语对应句式，且注意时态先后关系。

questions.stem: In the sentence "The importance of this discovery cannot be overemphasized," the most accurate Chinese translation of "cannot be overemphasized" is:
opts: 不能过分强调
怎么强调也不为过
无法被强调
不应该被强调
questions.explain: 考点：cannot...over-结构表'再……也不为过'，是英译汉中的特殊否定结构，直译'不能过分强调'为典型误译。

questions.stem: The phrase "a walk in the park" in "The exam was a walk in the park" should be translated as:
opts: 公园散步
轻而易举的事
在公园里走一走
公园漫步
questions.explain: 考点：英语习语'a walk in the park'在英译汉中不可字面直译，需转化为汉语对应习语'轻而易举'。

questions.stem: In "He is anything but a scholar," the correct Chinese translation is:
opts: 他什么都是，就是不是学者
他根本不是学者
他除了学者什么都是
他是一位学者
questions.explain: 考点：'anything but'结构表'根本不、绝不'，是英译汉中的否定转移现象，易误译为'除了……什么都是'。

questions.stem: The sentence "She was only too happy to help" should be translated as:
opts: 她只是太高兴了，所以不愿意帮忙
她非常乐意帮忙
她高兴得过分了，不愿帮忙
她只是很高兴去帮忙
questions.explain: 考点：'only too...to'结构表'非常……'，与'too...to'（太……而不能）相反，是英译汉中的易混结构。

questions.stem: In "It is a wise man that never makes mistakes," the best Chinese translation is:
opts: 聪明的人从不犯错
再聪明的人也会犯错
聪明的人不会犯错
只有聪明人才不犯错
questions.explain: 考点：'It is a + adj. + n. + that...'句型表让步否定，实际含义为'即使……也……'，不可按字面直译。

questions.stem: The phrase "as good as" in "He as good as admitted his guilt" should be translated as:
opts: 和……一样好
实际上、无异于
尽可能好地
和……一样优秀
questions.explain: 考点：'as good as'在英译汉中可表'实际上、几乎等于'，是固定短语，不可按比较级字面翻译。

questions.stem: In "I don't think it will rain today," the most idiomatic Chinese translation is:
opts: 我不认为今天会下雨
我认为今天不会下雨
我不觉得今天会下雨
今天不会下雨，我不这样认为
questions.explain: 考点：英译汉中否定转移现象——英语否定主句动词，汉语习惯否定从句，需调整语序符合汉语表达。

questions.stem: The sentence "He is the last person to tell a lie" should be translated as:
opts: 他是最后一个说谎的人
他绝不可能说谎
他最后才说谎
他是说谎最晚的人
questions.explain: 考点：'the last person to do'表'最不可能……的人'，是英译汉中的特殊否定表达，不可按字面译'最后一个'。

questions.stem: In "What he said is nothing less than a masterpiece," the correct translation of "nothing less than" is:
opts: 一点也不比……差
简直是、不亚于
比……少
与……无关
questions.explain: 考点：'nothing less than'表'简直是、不亚于'，是英译汉中的强调结构，易与'nothing more than'（仅仅）混淆。

questions.stem: The idiom "pull one's leg" in "Don't pull my leg, I know you're joking" should be translated as:
opts: 拉我的腿
拖我的后腿
开我的玩笑
扯我的后腿
questions.explain: 考点：英语习语'pull one's leg'意为'开玩笑、逗弄'，英译汉时不可直译为'拉腿'或与'拖后腿'混淆。

questions.stem: In the sentence "The importance of the project cannot be overemphasized," the most accurate Chinese translation is:
opts: 这个项目的重要性不能被过分强调。
这个项目的重要性怎么强调也不为过。
这个项目的重要性不能被过度重视。
这个项目的重要性无法被强调。
questions.explain: 考点：cannot...over- 结构应译为"再怎么……也不为过"，而非字面否定。

questions.stem: The phrase "a storm in a teacup" is best translated into Chinese as:
opts: 茶杯里的风暴
小题大做
杯水车薪
风平浪静
questions.explain: 考点：英语习语"a storm in a teacup"应意译为"小题大做"，保留比喻义而非字面直译。

questions.stem: In the sentence "He is anything but a scholar," the correct Chinese translation is:
opts: 他什么都是，就是不是一个学者。
他绝不是一个学者。
他除了学者什么都是。
他可能是一个学者。
questions.explain: 考点："anything but" 意为"绝不、根本不"，与"nothing but"（仅仅）相反。

questions.stem: The sentence "It is a wise man that never makes mistakes" should be translated into Chinese as:
opts: 聪明的人从不犯错误。
智者千虑，必有一失。
从不犯错误的人是聪明人。
聪明人也会犯错误。
questions.explain: 考点："It is a + adj. + n. that..." 句型常含让步意味，应译为"再……的人也难免……"。

questions.stem: The English expression "She was born with a silver spoon in her mouth" is best rendered in Chinese as:
opts: 她出生时嘴里含着银勺子。
她出身富贵。
她生来就喜欢银勺子。
她含着金汤匙出生。
questions.explain: 考点：英语习语"silver spoon"在中文中对应"金汤匙"（而非"银勺子"），需符合中文文化习惯。

questions.stem: In translating "I don't think it will rain today" into Chinese, the most natural rendering is:
opts: 我不认为今天会下雨。
我认为今天不会下雨。
我不觉得今天会下雨。
今天不会下雨，我不这么认为。
questions.explain: 考点：英语否定前置（否定主句）在汉译时应转换为否定从句（否定从句谓语），符合中文表达习惯。

questions.stem: The sentence "He was the last person to betray his country" should be translated as:
opts: 他是最后一个背叛祖国的人。
他绝不会背叛祖国。
他上次背叛了祖国。
他最后背叛了祖国。
questions.explain: 考点："the last person to do" 意为"最不可能做某事的人"，而非字面"最后一个"。

questions.stem: The English idiom "kill two birds with one stone" is best translated into Chinese as:
opts: 一石二鸟
一举两得
一箭双雕
一石击二鸟
questions.explain: 考点：英语"kill two birds with one stone"在中文中最对应的习语是"一箭双雕"，而非直译"一石二鸟"（虽可理解但非地道习语）。

questions.stem: The sentence "He is too careful not to have noticed the mistake" should be translated as:
opts: 他太粗心了，没有注意到这个错误。
他太细心了，不可能没注意到这个错误。
他太细心了，没有注意到这个错误。
他太粗心了，不可能注意到这个错误。
questions.explain: 考点："too...not to..." 结构为双重否定，表"太……以至于不会不……"，即肯定含义。

questions.stem: The sentence "What he said is all Greek to me" is best translated into Chinese as:
opts: 他说的对我来说全是希腊语。
他说的我一句也听不懂。
他说的全是关于希腊的事情。
他说的对我来说像天书一样。
questions.explain: 考点："Greek to me" 意为"完全不懂"，中文对应"天书"比直译"希腊语"更符合文化习惯。

questions.stem: In the sentence "It is not the consciousness of men that determines their being, but, on the contrary, their social being that determines their consciousness.", the most accurate Chinese translation of "on the contrary" is:
opts: 相反地
恰恰相反
反之
正相反
questions.explain: 考查英译汉中转折关系的准确表达。"on the contrary" 强调与前面所述完全对立，"恰恰相反" 语气最强、最贴合原文的辩证否定逻辑，而"相反地"和"反之"语气偏弱，"正相反"虽可接受但不如"恰恰相反"精准。

questions.stem: How should the phrase "the fabric of society" be best rendered in Chinese?
opts: 社会结构
社会织物
社会肌理
社会框架
questions.explain: 考查英译汉中隐喻的转化。"fabric" 本义为织物，在社科语境中喻指社会内在的有机组织与纹理，"社会肌理"既保留隐喻又符合中文表达，而"社会结构"偏静态、"社会框架"偏机械，"社会织物"则直译失当。

questions.stem: In translating "He is the last person to accept a bribe.", which Chinese version correctly conveys the original meaning?
opts: 他是最后一个接受贿赂的人。
他决不会接受贿赂。
他刚刚接受了贿赂。
他勉强接受了贿赂。
questions.explain: 考查英译汉中"the last + 名词 + to do"结构的否定含义。该结构表示"最不可能做某事的人"，而非字面的"最后一个"，属于典型的英语习惯表达，需转化为中文的否定句式才能准确达意。

questions.stem: The sentence "There is no denying that the policy has brought about significant changes." should be translated into Chinese as:
opts: 没有否认政策带来了显著变化。
不可否认，这项政策带来了显著变化。
否认政策带来显著变化是没有的。
政策带来了显著变化，这是没有否认的。
questions.explain: 考查英译汉中"There is no denying that..."固定句式的转化。该句式应译为"不可否认……"，这是中文中对应的惯用表达，其他选项均为生硬的直译或语序不当。

questions.stem: In the context of literary translation, how should the underlined part in "She was a study in contradictions — fierce yet tender, stubborn yet yielding." be best translated?
opts: 她是一个矛盾的研究
她是一个矛盾体
她是一项关于矛盾的研究
她研究矛盾
questions.explain: 考查英译汉中名词短语的灵活转化。"a study in contradictions" 是文学性表达，意为"一个充满矛盾的人/事物"，译为"矛盾体"既简洁又传神，直译"研究"则会完全偏离原意。

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most accurate Chinese translation of "The significance of the discovery was not lost on the scientific community."?
opts: 科学界没有丢失这一发现的意义。
科学界充分意识到了这一发现的重要性。
这一发现的意义没有被科学界丢失。
科学界对这一发现的意义并不在意。
questions.explain: 考查英译汉中双重否定的转化。"not lost on sb" 意为"被某人充分理解/意识到"，是英语中常见的双重否定表达，需转化为中文的肯定句式才能自然达意，直译"丢失"会造成语义错误。

questions.stem: In translating "It is a wise father that knows his own child." (from Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice), the correct Chinese rendering is:
opts: 一个聪明的父亲才认识自己的孩子。
再聪明的父亲也未必了解自己的孩子。
认识自己孩子的父亲是聪明的。
父亲了解自己的孩子是明智的。
questions.explain: 考查英译汉中"It is a + adj. + n. + that + 否定/条件"句型的反译。莎士比亚此句实为反讽，意为"即使再聪明的父亲也未必了解自己的孩子"，需转化为中文的反说句式，直译会完全误解原意。

questions.stem: How should the English idiom "to have a finger in every pie" be best translated into Chinese?
opts: 每个派里都插一根手指
多管闲事
什么事都插一手
贪得无厌
